sentences.zh: 五禮之別，二曰凶。

translations.literal: Of the five kinds of ritual, the second is called 'inauspicious' (mourning).
translations.idiomatic: Among the five canonical rituals, the second category is mourning for the dead.

sentences.zh: 自天子至於庶人，身體髮膚，受之父母，其理既均，其情亦等，生則養，死則哀，故曰三年之喪，天下之達禮者也。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, body, skin, and hair are received from father and mother; the principle is uniform and the feeling equal—in life they nurture, in death they mourn; therefore it is said that three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From the sovereign to the humblest subject, flesh and hair come from one's parents; the duty is the same and the grief no different—while they live we sustain them, when they die we mourn them. Hence the canon calls three years' mourning the rite that runs through all the world.

sentences.zh: 漢禮，天子崩，自不豫至於登遐及葬，喪紀之制，與夫三代變易。

translations.literal: Under Han ritual, when the Son of Heaven collapsed, from the first illness through the final journey to burial, the mourning regulations changed with the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Han court precedent for an emperor's death—from the first illness through the lying-in-state to interment—shifted its mourning code across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou models.

sentences.zh: 魏晉以來，大體同漢。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, the broad pattern matched Han.
translations.idiomatic: From the Wei through the Jin, the dynasty largely kept Han practice.

sentences.zh: 然自漢文革喪禮之制，後代遵之，無復三年之禮。

translations.literal: Yet from Emperor Wen of Han's reform of mourning regulations, later ages followed it and no longer practiced three years' mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once Emperor Wen of Han pared the mourning statutes, every succeeding age copied his shortcut, and the full three-year observance disappeared.

sentences.zh: 及魏武臨終，遺令「天下尚未安定，未得遵古。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu was near death, he left a command: 'All under Heaven is not yet settled; I cannot follow antiquity.'
translations.idiomatic: As Cao Cao lay dying, his testament read, 'The realm is still unsettled; we cannot return to ancient lengths of mourning.'

sentences.zh: 百官當臨中者，十五舉音，葬畢便除。

translations.literal: For the hundred officials who should attend at the central halt, raise the dirge fifteen times; when burial is finished, remove mourning at once.
translations.idiomatic: Officials attending the catafalque in the capital were to intone the pulling-hymn fifteen times, then shed mourning the moment the tomb was closed.

sentences.zh: 其將兵屯戍者，不得離部。

translations.literal: Those who command troops on garrison may not leave their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders holding field garrisons were forbidden to quit their posts.

sentences.zh: 」魏武以正月庚子崩，辛丑即殯，是月丁卯葬，是為不逾月也。

translations.literal: ' Wei Wu died on gengzi in the first month; on xinchou he was encoffined; on dingmao that same month he was buried—this is what is meant by 'not exceeding one month.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Cao Cao died on the gengzi day of the first month; by xinchou the bier stood ready; dingmao that same month saw the interment—mourning lifted inside a single month.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝、景帝之崩，並從權制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan and Emperor Jing died, each likewise followed the expedient code.
translations.idiomatic: The deaths of Sima Yi and Sima Shi were handled under the same shortened schedule.

sentences.zh: 文帝之崩，國內服三日。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen died, the realm observed mourning for three days only.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao died, the whole state wore mourning for three days and no more.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦遵漢魏之典，既葬除喪，然猶深衣素冠，降席撤膳。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu likewise followed Han and Wei precedent: once the burial ended he set aside formal mourning, yet still wore plain deep garments and an undyed cap, lowered his mat, and withdrew rich food from his table.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Sima Yan kept the Han–Wei rule of ending court mourning at burial, but he still dressed in plain hemp deep robes, set aside brocade cushions, and ate only coarse fare.

sentences.zh: 太宰司馬孚、太傅鄭沖、太保王祥、太尉何曾、司徒領中領軍司馬望、司空荀顗、車騎將軍賈充、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔、都護大將軍郭建、侍中郭綏、中書監荀勖、中軍將軍羊祜等奏曰：「臣聞禮典軌度，豐殺隨時，虞夏商周，咸不相襲，蓋有由也。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Sima Fu, Grand Tutor Zheng Chong, Grand Guardian Wang Xiang, Grand Commandant He Ceng, Minister of Education concurrently Central Army commander Sima Wang, Minister of Works Xun Yi, General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Wu Yan, Chief Protector and Grand General Guo Jian, Palace Attendant Guo Sui, Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu, Central Army General Yang Hu, and others memorialized: 'We have heard that ritual canons and measures wax or wane with the times; the houses of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou never blindly copied one another—each had its reasons.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fu, Zheng Chong, Wang Xiang, He Ceng, Sima Wang, Xun Yi, Jia Chong, Pei Xiu, Wu Yan, Guo Jian, Guo Sui, Xun Xu, Yang Hu, and the rest jointly wrote: 'Canonical ritual scales with the age; the Five Emperors and Three Kings changed their music and ceremonies because circumstance, not caprice, demanded it.'

sentences.zh: 大晉紹承漢魏，有革有因，期於足以興化而已，故未得皆返太素，同規上古也。

translations.literal: Great Jin inherits Han and Wei with some reforms and some continuities, aiming only to lift custom where it must; therefore it cannot yet return wholesale to pristine antiquity or match high antiquity in a single stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Our Jin dynasty picks up Han and Wei practice where it still serves and alters it where it does not, intent solely on renewing the people—it cannot snap every tie to recent precedent and pretend to be the Yellow Emperor's court.

sentences.zh: 陛下既以俯遵漢魏降喪之典，以濟時務，而躬蹈大孝，情過乎哀，素冠深衣，降席撤膳，雖武丁行之于殷世，曾閔履之於布衣，未足以逾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already bowed to Han and Wei's lowered mourning canons to meet pressing affairs, yet you personally tread the utmost filial path; your feeling overshoots moderation—plain cap, deep garments, lowered mat, curtailed meals—even King Wuding in the Yin age or Zengzi and Min Ziqian as commoners did not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: You have accepted the shortened mourning of Han and Wei for the sake of state, yet you still live like the most scrupulous mourner—undyed cap, hemp robes, mat on the ground, plain gruel—surpassing even King Wuding of Shang or Zeng and Min in their scholar's cottages.

sentences.zh: 方今荊蠻未夷，庶政未乂，萬機事殷，動勞神慮，豈遑全遂聖旨，以從至情。

translations.literal: Now the southern tribes are not yet pacified, government is not yet ordered, and myriad threads of business press upon you, taxing mind and spirit—how could you wholly indulge sage intent and the utmost of private feeling?
translations.idiomatic: The southern rebels are still in the field, every office clamors for decisions, and the red basket never empties—your spirit cannot bear both the realm and unbroken vigil grief.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為陛下宜割情以康時濟俗，輒敕御府易服，內省改坐，太官復膳，諸所施行，皆如舊制。

translations.literal: We your servants therefore believe Your Majesty should cut private feeling to heal the age and aid custom; we dare order the Palace Treasury to exchange garments, the inner apartments to restore seating, the Grand Provisioner to restore full meals, and every other measure to follow the standing regulations.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to steady the times by checking private sorrow: let the wardrobe send court dress again, the inner chambers raise the cushions, the kitchens resume regular meals—everything as statute prescribes before the altars starve for attention.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「每感念幽冥，而不得終苴絰於草土，以存此痛，況當食稻衣錦，誠詭然激切其心，非所以相解也。

translations.literal: ' The edict replied: 'Whenever I brood on the shades below and realize I cannot finish wearing straw cord on the burial mound to keep this pain alive—how much more to eat polished rice and wear brocade—indeed it stabs the heart; that is no way to console myself.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor answered: 'Each time I think of my father under the earth and know I cannot keep the rough cord on the fresh tumulus, the wound opens anew; to don silk and eat white rice would twist the knife—no salve for grief.'

sentences.zh: 吾本諸生家，傳禮來久，何心一旦便易此情於所天！

translations.literal: I was born to a house of scholars; the rites have been handed down among us a long time—how could my heart one morning cast off this feeling toward him who is my heaven!
translations.idiomatic: I was raised a classicist family; ritual has shaped us for generations—how could I overnight blunt love for the man who gave me life?'

sentences.zh: 相從已多，可試省孔子答宰我之言，無事紛紜也。

translations.literal: You have followed me long; try reviewing Confucius's answer to Zai Wo—do not fuss at me again and again.
translations.idiomatic: You have served at my side for years—reread the Master's rebuke of Zai Wo and spare me another round of pleas.'

sentences.zh: 言及悲剝，柰何！

translations.literal: When words touch grief it tears the heart—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Speech only tears the wound wider—what am I to do?'

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏：「伏讀聖詔，感以悲懷，輒思仲尼所以抑宰我之問，聖思所以不能已已，甚深甚篤。

translations.literal: ' Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have read the sage edict and are moved to grief; we reflect on why Confucius checked Zai Wo's question—the sage mind cannot stop itself; the feeling is very deep and very earnest.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Sima Fu's party wrote again: 'We lay your sacred words on our hearts and weep; we remember how Confucius trimmed Zai Wo's demand for a one-year mourning—a sage's grief will not obey a calendar, and yours runs deeper still.'

sentences.zh: 然今者干戈未戢，武事未偃，萬機至重，天下至眾。

translations.literal: Yet now weapons are not yet stilled, military affairs not yet rested, the myriad threads are weightiest, and all under Heaven is most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet spears are still crossed, campaigns unfinished, and the realm's business outweighs every private claim.

sentences.zh: 陛下以萬乘之尊，履布衣之禮，服粗席稿，水飲疏食，殷憂內盈，毀悴外表。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in the honor of ten thousand chariots treads the rites of a commoner—coarse mat and straw padding, drinking water and eating coarse food, sorrow swelling within, emaciation showing without.
translations.idiomatic: You who command the empire sleep on straw, drink plain water, and waste visibly away while grief eats you from within.

sentences.zh: 而躬勤萬機，坐而待旦，降心接下，仄不遑食，所以勞力者如斯之甚。

translations.literal: Yet you personally toil at myriad threads of state, sit awaiting dawn, humble your heart to receive subordinates, and lean so far you have no leisure to eat—such labor of strength is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still hold dawn audience, humble yourself before ministers, and skip meals to finish memorials—no body could endure the strain.

sentences.zh: 是以臣等悚息不寧，誠懼神氣用損，以疚大事。

translations.literal: Therefore we your servants tremble and breathe uneasily, truly fearing that spirit will be depleted and the great affair harmed.
translations.idiomatic: We tremble lest your spirit snap and the dynasty pay the price.

sentences.zh: 輒敕有司，改坐復常，率由舊典。

translations.literal: We dare order the relevant offices to restore your seat and routine, following the old canons.
translations.idiomatic: Order the bureaus to restore your cushions, meals, and court dress under the standing code.'

sentences.zh: 惟陛下察納愚款，以慰皇太后之心。

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty examine and accept our foolish sincerity, so as to console the heart of the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Only accept our clumsy plea and give the empress dowager peace of mind.'

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「重覽奏議，益以悲剝，不能自勝，柰何！

translations.literal: ' Another edict said: 'Rereading your memorials only deepens the tearing grief; I cannot master myself—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: ' Another rescript ran: 'Each rereading of your papers rips the wound—I cannot steady myself—what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What can be done!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?'

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，自古達禮，誠聖人稱情立衷，明恕而行也。

translations.literal: Three years' mourning has from antiquity been the penetrating rite of the realm; truly the sages weighed human feeling, set the inner mean, and acted with enlightened forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Three years' mourning is the rite that runs through all ages: the sages framed it from genuine grief, set a middle path, and taught forbearance in its observance.'

sentences.zh: 神靈日遠，無所訴告，雖薄於情，食旨服美，所不堪也。

translations.literal: The spirits grow daily more distant; there is nowhere to cry complaint—though the outward show be slight, to taste rich food and wear fine cloth is unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: The dead recede day by day with nowhere to pour complaint; even if court dress stayed thin, rich flavors and brocade would choke me.'

sentences.zh: 不宜反覆，重傷其心，言用斷絕，柰何！

translations.literal: You ought not go back and forth and doubly wound this heart; I break off words—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: Do not harry me and tear the scab again—I end here—what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What can be done!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?'

sentences.zh: 」帝遂以此禮終三年。

translations.literal: ' The emperor therefore observed mourning to the full three years under this rite.
translations.idiomatic: ' With that he carried the full three-year vigil despite every plea.

sentences.zh: 後居太后之喪亦如之。

translations.literal: Later, when mourning the Empress Dowager, he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated the same austerity when the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔曰：「此上旬，先帝棄天下日也，便以周年。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict said: 'In this first decad falls the anniversary of the late emperor's passing—thus a full cycle is complete.'
translations.idiomatic: An eighth-month edict noted that the first third of the month marked a year since his father's death.

sentences.zh: 吾煢煢，當復何時一得敘人子之情邪！

translations.literal: I stand utterly alone—when shall I once exhaust a son's proper feeling!
translations.idiomatic: I am left desolate—when may I ever discharge a son's debt of grief?'

sentences.zh: 思慕煩毒，欲詔陵瞻侍，以盡哀憤。

translations.literal: Longing and grief burn within; I wish to order attendance at the mausoleum to exhaust sorrow and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Longing gnaws me; I mean to visit the tumulus and pour out this ache.'

sentences.zh: 主者具行備。

translations.literal: Let the supervisor prepare the full arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Let the steward draw up the procession at once.'

sentences.zh: 」太宰安平王孚、尚書令裴秀、尚書僕射武陔等奏：「陛下至孝蒸蒸，哀思罔極。

translations.literal: ' Grand Preceptor the Prince of Anping, Fu, Prefect of the Masters of Writing Pei Xiu, Vice Minister Wu Yan, and others memorialized: 'Your Majesty's utmost filiality steams upward; mourning thought knows no limit.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Sima Fu, Pei Xiu, Wu Yan, and their colleagues answered: 'Your filial steam rises to Heaven; grief has no boundary for you.'

sentences.zh: 衰麻雖除，哀毀疏食，有損神和。

translations.literal: Though hemp garments are removed, grief-destroyed coarse eating still injures inner harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Court hemp is gone, yet you still fast like a mourner and harm your inner balance.'

sentences.zh: 今雖秋節，尚有餘暑，謁見山陵，悲感摧傷，群下竊用竦息，以為宜降抑聖情，以慰萬國。

translations.literal: Now, though the season is autumn, residual heat remains; if you visit the hill-tomb, sorrow would crush and wound you; your subordinates secretly tremble and believe you ought to moderate sage feeling so as to console the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn heat still lingers; a journey to the mausoleum would shatter your health—we beg you to bridle sacred sorrow for the realm's sake.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「孤煢忽爾，日月已周，痛慕摧感，永無逮及。

translations.literal: ' The edict said: 'I stand orphaned in a flash; sun and moon have completed their round; pain and longing crush me—forever unable to catch up.
translations.idiomatic: ' The throne replied: 'Orphaned in an instant, a year already gone—grief outruns every chance to atone.'

sentences.zh: 欲瞻奉山陵，以敘哀憤，體氣自佳耳。

translations.literal: I wish to gaze upon and attend the hill-tomb so as to vent sorrow and rage—my vital breath is naturally sound.
translations.idiomatic: I need only to stand at the tomb and voice this ache—my body is still strong enough.'

sentences.zh: 又已涼，便當行，不得如所奏也。

translations.literal: It has also turned cool; I ought to go—I cannot do as you memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The air has cooled; I am going—your plea cannot stand.'

sentences.zh: 主者便具行備。

translations.literal: Let the supervisor at once prepare the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Have the steward ready the train immediately.'

sentences.zh: 」又詔曰：「漢文不使天下盡哀，亦帝王至謙之志。

translations.literal: ' Another edict said: 'Emperor Wen of Han did not make all under Heaven exhaust mourning—that too expresses an emperor's utmost modest intent.
translations.idiomatic: ' A second edict added: 'Han Wendi spared the realm a full three years—that was imperial self-effacement, not indifference.'

sentences.zh: 當見山陵，何心而無服，其以衰絰行。

translations.literal: When I see the hill-tomb, how could my heart bear having no mourning dress? I shall proceed wearing zhui cords.
translations.idiomatic: Facing my father's mound without hemp would shame a son—I will travel in zhui mourning cords.'

sentences.zh: 」孚等重奏曰：「臣聞上古喪期無數，後世乃有年月之漸。

translations.literal: ' Fu and the others rememorialized: 'We have heard that in high antiquity mourning periods had no fixed count; later ages gradually introduced years and months.
translations.idiomatic: ' They shot back: 'Antiquity set no fixed mourning tally; only later did calendars of months appear.'

sentences.zh: 漢文帝隨時之義，制為短喪，傳之於後。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han, according to the right meaning of his times, established short mourning and handed it down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wendi shortened mourning to suit his crisis, and every dynasty since copied him.'

sentences.zh: 陛下以社稷宗廟之重，萬方億兆之故，既從權制，釋除衰麻，群臣百姓吉服，今者謁陵，以敘哀慕，若加衰絰，進退無當。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, for the weight of the altars of soil and grain and ancestral shrines and for the sake of the myriad regions and hundred million people, has already followed the expedient regulation and removed hemp; many ministers and commoners wear auspicious dress—now, to visit the tomb and order sorrow, if you add zhui cords, advance and retreat would lack proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: You laid aside hemp for the altars' sake while the court already wears bright dress; to wind cord again for the ride to the tomb would leave neither mourning nor felicity coherent.'

sentences.zh: 不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: We do not dare accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot obey that rescript.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「亦知不在此麻布耳。

translations.literal: ' The edict said: 'I also know the point is not this bolt of hemp alone.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor answered: 'I know the issue is not the cloth itself.'

sentences.zh: 然人子情思，為欲令哀喪之物在身，蓋近情也。

translations.literal: Yet a son's intent in feeling wishes the tokens of mourning to stay on the body—roughly that is what draws close to true feeling.
translations.idiomatic: A child simply wants the outward signs of grief on his skin—that is what feels honest.'

sentences.zh: 群臣自當案舊制。

translations.literal: The many ministers ought themselves to follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers will keep the standing dress code among themselves.'

sentences.zh: 」孚等又奏曰：「臣聞聖人制作，必從時宜。

translations.literal: ' Fu and the others again memorialized: 'We have heard that when sages establish institutions they always follow the right fit of the times.
translations.idiomatic: ' Sima Fu's bloc wrote again: 'The sages never framed ritual without watching the times.'

sentences.zh: 故五帝殊樂，三王異禮，此古今所以不同，質文所以迭用也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Five Emperors had different music and the Three Kings had different rites—this is why ancient and modern differ and substance and ornament alternate.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors changed their music, the Three Kings their ceremonies—substance and polish shift because history shifts.'

sentences.zh: 陛下隨時之宜，既降心克己，俯就權制，既除衰麻，而行心喪之禮，今復制服，義無所依。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, according to the right fit of the times, has already lowered mind and restrained self, bowed to expedient regulation, removed hemp, and practiced the rite of mourning in the heart; now to don mourning garments again has no basis in ritual meaning.
translations.idiomatic: You already accepted the shortened code and mourned in heart while court dress brightened; to reclothe in hemp now would contradict the very expedient you approved.'

sentences.zh: 若君服而臣不服，亦未之敢安也。

translations.literal: If the lord wears mourning while ministers do not, we likewise dare not rest easy in that.
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign wore hemp while ministers wore silk, we could not call the court at ease either.'

sentences.zh: 參議宜如前奏。

translations.literal: After deliberation, we believe you should follow the prior memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation confirms our earlier plea.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「患情不能跂及耳，衣服何在。

translations.literal: ' The edict said: 'The trouble is that feeling cannot reach that far—what are clothes after all?
translations.idiomatic: ' He answered: 'My grief cannot stretch to every symbol—what are robes beside that?'

sentences.zh: 諸君勤勤之至，豈苟相違。」

translations.literal: Your gentlemen's earnestness reaches the utmost—how could I lightly oppose you.'
translations.idiomatic: Your zeal is utter—how could I trifle with your loyalty?'

sentences.zh: ，皇太后崩。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] The Empress Dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: Next the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「前代故事，倚廬中施白縑帳、蓐、素床，以布巾裹塊草，軺輦、版輿、細犢車皆施縑裏。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized: 'Precedent of former ages: in the mourning lean-to hang white thin-silk curtains, rush mats, and plain beds; wrap clods in plain cloth on straw; line light carriages, plank litters, and small ox carts with thin silk.'
translations.idiomatic: Authorities cited old practice: the mourning hut should have white gauze hangings, rush mat, plain couch, straw with cloth-wrapped clods, and silk-lined hearses and wagons.'

sentences.zh: 」詔不聽，但令以布衣車而已，其餘居喪之制，不改禮文。

translations.literal: ' The edict did not consent; it ordered only plain-cloth carts; as for the rest of the dwelling-in-mourning system, it did not alter the ritual text.
translations.idiomatic: ' He refused the silks but allowed plain carts only, leaving every other mourning rule as written in the canon.'

sentences.zh: 有司又奏：「大行皇太后當以四月二十五日安厝。

translations.literal: The offices again memorialized: 'The late great empress dowager ought on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth month be laid in the side chamber.'
translations.idiomatic: They proposed burying the late empress dowager on the twenty-fifth of the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 故事，虞著衰服，既虞而除。

translations.literal: Precedent: at the Yu rite one wears qi-cui; once the Yu is completed, one removes it.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent required qi-cui hemp until the Yu rite, then doffing.

sentences.zh: 其內外官僚皆就朝晡臨位，御除服訖，各還所次除衰服。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials all attend mourning at dawn and dusk; when the court finishes removing mourning, each returns to his station and removes qi garments.
translations.idiomatic: All ranks were to wail morning and evening at court, then shed qi dress when the sovereign ended mourning.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「夫三年之喪，天下之達禮也。

translations.literal: ' The edict said: 'Three years' mourning is the penetrating rite of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ' The rescript read: 'Three years' mourning is the rite that runs through all the world.'

sentences.zh: 受終身之愛，而無數年之報，柰何葬而便即吉，情所不忍也。

translations.literal: Receiving a lifetime's love yet repaying it without several years—how can we at burial then at once go auspicious? What the feeling cannot bear.'
translations.idiomatic: You receive a parent's love for life yet repay it in less than a handful of years—how could I snap to felicity the day the coffin drops? My heart will not bear it.'

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏：「世有險易，道有洿隆，所遇之時異，誠有由然，非忽禮也。

translations.literal: ' The offices again memorialized: 'Generations have peril and ease; the Way has high and low—what one meets in the season differs, and indeed there is reason for it; it is not spurning ritual.
translations.idiomatic: ' They pressed again: 'Times differ in danger and calm, the Way rises and falls—each age has its excuse without scorning the rites themselves.'

sentences.zh: 方今戎馬未散，王事至殷，更須聽斷，以熙庶績。

translations.literal: Now war-horses are not yet dispersed, royal business is most pressing; still more must you hear lawsuits so as to brighten the myriad threads.
translations.idiomatic: Armies still march, the vermilion basket overflows—you must judge suits to keep the realm lit.'

sentences.zh: 昔周康王始登翌室，猶戴冕臨朝。

translations.literal: Formerly, when King Kang of Zhou first ascended the wing chamber, he still wore the court crown and held court.
translations.idiomatic: King Kang of Zhou took the mourning chamber yet still donned court regalia for audiences.'

sentences.zh: 降于漢魏，既葬除釋，諒闇之禮，自遠代而廢矣。

translations.literal: Down to Han and Wei, after burial came removal and release; the rite of silent seclusion (liang'an) has been abandoned since remote generations.
translations.idiomatic: By Han and Wei, mourning ended at burial and the "palled silence" of high antiquity was long gone.'

sentences.zh: 惟陛下割高宗之制，從當時之宜。

translations.literal: Only let Your Majesty cut the Gaozong system and follow the right fit of the present time.
translations.idiomatic: We beg you to trim the Shang king's example and bend to today's need.'

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「夫三年之喪，所以盡情致禮，葬已便除，所不堪也。

translations.literal: ' The edict said: 'Three years' mourning is the means to exhaust feeling and complete ritual—to remove it once burial is done is what the feeling cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: ' He answered: 'Three years exist to spend grief completely—doffing at the grave tears the heart.'

sentences.zh: 當敘吾哀懷，言用斷絕，柰何！

translations.literal: I should narrate my sorrow—words break off—what can be done!
translations.idiomatic: I meant to speak my sorrow but words fail—what can I do?'

sentences.zh: 柰何！

translations.literal: What can be done!
translations.idiomatic: What can I do?'

sentences.zh: 」有司又固請。

translations.literal: ' The offices again firmly requested.
translations.idiomatic: ' The bureaus petitioned again, harder.'

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「不能篤孝，勿以毀傷為憂也。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'If I cannot practice deep filiality, do not take ruin and injury as your worry.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'If I cannot be a perfect mourner, do not fret over my wasting away.'

sentences.zh: 誠知衣服末事耳，然今思存草土，率當以吉物奪之，乃所以重傷至心，非見念也。

translations.literal: I truly know clothes are the least of matters—yet now I wish to remain on straw soil, and if you would take that away with auspicious things, that doubles the wound to the utmost mind; it is not true care.
translations.idiomatic: I know silk is a small thing—but while I mean to stay on the burial mound you would strip me with bright gear; that gouges the heart, not heals it.'

sentences.zh: 每代禮典質文皆不同耳，何為限以近制，使達喪闕然乎！

translations.literal: Each age's ritual canon differs in substance and pattern—why should I be bound by recent regulation and leave penetrating mourning empty!
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty's code mixes plain and polished—why nail me to recent statute and hollow the great mourning?'

sentences.zh: 」群臣又固請，帝流涕久之乃許。

translations.literal: ' The many ministers again firmly requested; the emperor wept a long time and then consented.
translations.idiomatic: ' Ministers pressed until he wept long and yielded.'

sentences.zh: 文明皇后崩及武元楊后崩，天下將吏發哀三日止。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Wenming died and when Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, officers throughout the realm raised mourning for three days and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Yuan died and when Empress Yang the consort of Wu died, officers empire-wide wailed three days only.'

sentences.zh: 穆帝崩，哀帝立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mu died, Emperor Ai was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai succeeded when Emperor Mu passed.

sentences.zh: 帝于穆帝為從父昆弟，穆帝舅褚歆有表，中書答表朝廷無其儀，詔下議。

translations.literal: The emperor toward Emperor Mu was a father's-brother's son; Emperor Mu's maternal uncle Chu Xin submitted a memorial; the Secretariat replied to the memorial that the court had no such precedent, and an edict sent the matter down for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was Mu's cousin; Mu's uncle Chu Xin asked how to mourn; the Secretariat said no rule existed and the throne sent the case to debate.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射江虨等四人並云，閔僖兄弟也，而為父子，則哀帝應為帝嗣。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Jiang Pin and four others together said: 'Duke Min and Duke Xi were brothers yet treated as father and son—therefore Emperor Ai ought to follow the emperor's line of succession.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pin and four others cited Duke Min and Duke Xi of Lu—brothers treated as father and son—and argued Ai should continue Cheng's line.

sentences.zh: 衛軍王述等二十五人云「成帝不私親愛，越授天倫，康帝受命顯宗。

translations.literal: General of the Guards Wang Shu and twenty-five others said: 'Emperor Cheng did not show partiality to close kin but crossed the heavenly order to invest another; Emperor Kang received the mandate from Emperor Yuan.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu and twenty-five ministers said Cheng deliberately bypassed a natural heir and gave the throne to Kang, who derived his mandate from Yuan (Xianzong).

sentences.zh: 社稷之重，已移所授，纂承之序，宜繼康皇。

translations.literal: The weight of the altars was already transferred in the investiture; the order of succession ought to continue Emperor Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The altars had already passed on that branch, so succession should stay with Kang's line.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書謝奉等六人云：「繼體之正，宜本天屬，考之人情，宜繼顯宗也。

translations.literal: ' Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie Feng and six others said: 'The correct line of succession ought to take heaven-born tie as root; judging by human feeling, one ought to continue Emperor Yuan.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Xie Feng and six others argued the true thread follows blood, so Ai should continue Yuan (Xianzong).'

sentences.zh: 」詔從述等議，上繼顯宗。

translations.literal: ' The edict followed Wang Shu and the others' debate and ordered succession to continue Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: ' The edict sided with Wang Shu and made Ai heir to Emperor Yuan.'

sentences.zh: 七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Emperor Jianwen died—the second full mourning cycle met an intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Emperor Jianwen died just as the second mourning round collided with an intercalary month.

sentences.zh: 博士謝攸、孔粲議：「魯襄二十八年十二月乙未，楚子卒，實閏月而言十二月者，附正於前月也。

translations.literal: Erudites Xie You and Kong Can debated: 'In Lu Xiang's twenty-eighth year, on yiwei of the twelfth month the viscount of Chu died—it was really an intercalary month yet the text says twelfth month, meaning attach the correction to the preceding month.'
translations.idiomatic: Doctors Xie You and Kong Can cited the Spring and Autumn: Chu ruler's death dated to the twelfth month's yiwei though the month was intercalary—scribes pinned it to the prior standard month.'

sentences.zh: 喪事先遠，則應用博士吳商之言，以閏月祥。

translations.literal: Mourning affairs put the distant first—then one ought to adopt Erudite Wu Shang's opinion and use the intercalary month for the xiang rite.
translations.idiomatic: Because funeral timing favors the remote month, they urged adopting Wu Shang and holding the xiang in the leap month.'

sentences.zh: 」尚書僕射謝安、中領軍王劭、散騎常侍鄭襲、右衛將軍殷康、驍騎將軍袁宏、散騎侍郎殷茂、中書郎車胤、左丞劉遵、吏部郎劉耽意皆同。

translations.literal: ' Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing Xie An, Central Army commander Wang Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary Zheng Xi, General of the Right Guard Yin Kang, General of Swift Cavalry Yuan Hong, Cavalier Gentleman Yin Mao, Palace Secretariat Secretary Che Yin, Left Assistant Liu Zun, Personnel Section chief Liu Dan—all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: ' Xie An, Wang Shao, Zheng Xi, Yin Kang, Yuan Hong, Yin Mao, Che Yin, Liu Zun, and Liu Dan concurred.'

sentences.zh: 康曰：「過七月而未及八月，豈可謂之逾期。

translations.literal: Kang said: 'Having passed the seventh month and not yet reached the eighth—how can we call that overdue?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kang said passing the seventh without entering the eighth was not yet "past term."'

sentences.zh: 必所不了，則當從其重者。

translations.literal: If something cannot be decided, then one ought to follow the heavier alternative.
translations.idiomatic: When doubt remains, choose the stricter reading.'

sentences.zh: 」宏曰：「假值閏十二月而不取者，此則歲未終，固不可得矣。

translations.literal: Hong said: 'Suppose the case hits an intercalary twelfth month and one does not take it—then the year is not ended and it indeed cannot be obtained.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong added that skipping an intercalary twelfth would leave the ritual year unfinished—so the stricter reckoning could not be met.'

sentences.zh: 《漢書》以閏為後九月，明其同體也。

translations.literal: The Book of Han treats the intercalary month as the 'later ninth month,' clarifying that it is reckoned as the same ritual month as the ninth.
translations.idiomatic: The Han History classifies a leap month as a 'trailing ninth month,' showing it belongs to the same ritual body as the ninth.

sentences.zh: 」襲曰：「中宗、肅祖皆以閏月崩，祥除之變皆用閏之後月。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xi said: 'Zhongzong and Suzong both died in intercalary months; for the change of xiang removal they all used the month after the intercalary.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Xi noted that both Zhongzong and Suzong died in leap months, and each time the court ended the xiang observance in the month following the leap.'

sentences.zh: 先朝尚用閏之後月，今閏附七月，取之何疑，亦合遠日申情之言。

translations.literal: The prior court still used the month after the intercalary; now the leap attaches to the seventh month—what doubt is there in taking it? It also fits the maxim of choosing a distant day to give feeling full expression.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier regimes still counted the month after the leap; now the leap rides on the seventh month—there is no real ambiguity in adopting it, and it honors the classic preference for a remote mourning day.'

sentences.zh: 又閏是後七而非八也，豈逾月之嫌乎！

translations.literal: Moreover a leap month is a 'seventh after' rather than an eighth—how could there be any suspicion of having overshot the month!'
translations.idiomatic: A leap slot is still the seventh span, not an eighth, so it cannot count as 'over the month.'"'

sentences.zh: 」尚書令王彪之、侍中王混、中丞譙王恬、右丞戴謐等議異，彪之曰：「吳商中才小官，非名賢碩儒、公輔重臣、為時所準則者。

translations.literal: ' Minister of the Masters of Writing Wang Bianzhi, Palace Attendant Wang Hun, Palace Secretary the Prince of Qiao Wang Tian, Right Assistant Dai Mi, and others argued differently; Bianzhi said: 'Wu Shang is middling talent in a petty post—not a famed worthy or great scholar, not a pillar minister whom the age takes as its standard.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Wang Bianzhi, Wang Hun, Wang Tian, Dai Mi, and their party dissented: Wu Shang was a middling clerk, not a canonical authority the realm should treat as precedent.'

sentences.zh: 又取閏無證據，直攬遠日之義，越祥忌，限外取，不合卜遠之理。

translations.literal: Moreover adopting the leap month lacks textual proof—he simply seizes the gloss on choosing a distant day, crosses the xiang taboo, and grabs a date outside the limit, which violates the logic of divining for a remote day.'
translations.idiomatic: He cites no canonical warrant for the leap, twists the 'distant day' rule, and overruns the xiang boundary—nothing in divination theory supports that.'

sentences.zh: 又丞相桓公嘗論云，《禮》二十五月大祥。

translations.literal: Moreover Chancellor Duke Huan once argued that the Rites prescribe the great xiang in the twenty-fifth month.'
translations.idiomatic: Grand Duke Huan Wen had already argued the canon fixes the great xiang at month twenty-five.'

sentences.zh: 何緣越期取閏，乃二十六月乎？

translations.literal: What warrant is there to cross the full cycle and seize a leap month, making it the twenty-sixth month?'
translations.idiomatic: Why leap the boundary to a twenty-sixth month at all?'

sentences.zh: 」於是啟曰：「或以閏附七月，宜用閏月除者。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon they presented: 'Some hold that because the leap attaches to the seventh month, one ought use the leap month for removal.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The memorial went on: some said the leap belongs to the seventh month, so mourning should end in that leap.'

sentences.zh: 或以閏名雖除七月，而實以三旬別為一月，故應以七月除者。

translations.literal: ' Some hold that although the leap's name removes it from the seventh month, in reality three full decad periods form a separate month—therefore one ought remove mourning in the seventh month.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Others said the leap is only a third decad hung on the seventh, so the seventh month itself should still govern removal.'

sentences.zh: 臣等與中軍將軍沖參詳，一代大禮，宜準經典。

translations.literal: ' We your servants deliberated with Central Army General Sima Chong: a dynasty's great mourning must take the classics as its measure.'
translations.idiomatic: ' We joined Sima Chong, commander of the central army, and agreed that state ritual must track the canon.'

sentences.zh: 三年之喪，十三月而練，二十五月而畢，《禮》之明文也。

translations.literal: ' Three years' mourning: lian in the thirteenth month, completion in the twenty-fifth month—this is explicit text in the Rites.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Mourning Garments canon is plain: the lian falls in month thirteen, the full rite closes in month twenty-five.'

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，閏在年內，則略而不數。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn of Jin (Sun Sheng) holds that when a leap month falls inside the year, one omits it and does not count it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng's Jin Yang-qiu says intercalary months inside the ritual year are skipped in the tally.

sentences.zh: 明閏在年外，則不應取之以越期忌之重，禮制祥除必正期月故也。

translations.literal: This clarifies that when the leap lies outside the year, one must not seize it to cross the weight of the full-cycle taboo—ritual rules for ending the xiang must fix the correct month.'
translations.idiomatic: When the leap sits outside the mourning year, using it would violate the gravest intercalary taboo, because xiang removal must anchor on the true month count.'

sentences.zh: 」己酉晦，帝除縞即吉。

translations.literal: ' On jiyou, the last day of the month, the emperor shed mourning white silk and returned to auspicious dress.'
translations.idiomatic: ' On jiyou, month-end, the sovereign left white mourning and resumed felicity garb.'

sentences.zh: 徐廣論曰：「凡辨義詳理，無顯據明文可以折中奪易，則非疑如何。

translations.literal: Xu Guang reflected: 'Whenever one parses doctrine and logic, if there is no manifest proof or clear text by which to arbitrate change—then what is not doubtful?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang later wrote that without explicit scripture you cannot overturn settled mourning math.'

sentences.zh: 禮疑從重，喪易甯戚，順情通物，固有成言矣。

translations.literal: Ritual in doubt follows the heavier option; mourning may change, yet better show sorrow—accord feeling and penetrate things—indeed there are settled sayings on this.'
translations.idiomatic: When ritual is uncertain, choose the stricter reading; easing mourning should still privilege grief—antiquity already said as much.'

sentences.zh: 彪之不能徵援正義，有以相屈，但以名位格人，君子虛受，心無適莫，豈其然哉！

translations.literal: Bianzhi could not cite correct meaning to refute them—only used name and rank to box people in—a gentleman's mind should receive openly without partial favor—can it really be so!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bianzhi never proved his case on the merits—he appealed to rank—and a gentleman does not settle scholarship by office.'

sentences.zh: 執政從而行之，其殆過矣。」

translations.literal: The ruling power followed and enacted it—probably that overshot the mark.'"
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his line anyway—likely a mistake.'"

sentences.zh: 魏武以正月崩，魏文以其年七月設妓樂百戲，是則魏不以喪廢樂也。

translations.literal: Wei Wu died in the first month; Wei Wen in that year's seventh month set singing-girls and the hundred entertainments—therefore Wei did not cancel music because of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao died in the first month; Cao Pi still staged troupes and acrobats that seventh month—so Wei never treated mourning as a reason to silence the bands.

sentences.zh: 武帝以來，國有大喪，輒廢樂終三年。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu onward, whenever the state had great mourning, court music was suspended for the full three years.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Sima Yan, every dynastic bereavement silenced the orchestras for three years.

sentences.zh: 惠帝太安元年，太子喪未除，及元會亦廢樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taian under Emperor Hui, the crown prince's mourning was not yet removed—yet for the New Year court assembly music was likewise suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Hui's Taian era, while the heir still wore mourning, the Yuan-day levee went without music.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和中，為中原山陵未修復，頻年元會廢樂。

translations.literal: During Yonghe under Emperor Mu, because the imperial tombs on the Central Plain were not yet repaired, for successive years the Yuan assembly suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: Yonghe years saw the New Year court go silent while Luoyang's tombs lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 是時太后臨朝，后父褚裒薨，元會又廢樂也。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager presided at court; the empress's father Chu Pou died—the Yuan assembly again suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: The regent's father Chu Pou died that same span, so the levee stayed mute again.

sentences.zh: 孝武，為皇后王氏喪，亦廢樂。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu, mourning Empress Wang, likewise suspended music.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang died, Xiaowu ordered the same musical abstention.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，太傅錄尚書會稽王道子議：「山陵之後，通婚嫁不得作樂，以一期為斷。」

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died, Grand Tutor concurrently recording Masters of Writing the Prince of Guiji, Sima Daozi, debated: 'After the imperial tomb is closed, weddings may proceed but without music—take one full cycle as the limit.'"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi ruled that after the mausoleum sealed, commoners might marry but not hire musicians until a year had passed.'"

sentences.zh: 漢儀，太皇太后、皇太后崩，長樂太僕、少府大長秋典喪事，三公奉制度，他皆如禮。

translations.literal: Han regulations: when the grand empress dowager or empress dowager died, the Director of Changle, the Grand Coachman, the Grand Provisioner, and the Greater Chief of Staff managed funeral affairs; the Three Dukes presented the statutory scheme; everything else followed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Han statute put the inner-palace stewards in charge of a dowager's obsequies while the Three Dukes supplied the legal template.

sentences.zh: 魏晉亦同天子之儀。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin likewise matched the Son of Heaven's observances.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin copied the same imperial funeral code.

sentences.zh: ，武元楊皇后崩，及將遷于峻陽陵，依舊制，既葬，帝及群臣除喪即吉。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] When Empress Wu-Yuan Yang died, and when she was about to be moved to the Junyang mausoleum, according to old precedent, once burial ended the emperor and all ministers removed mourning and returned to auspicious dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Yang was conveyed to the Junyang tomb, the standing rule had everyone shed mourning the moment the vault closed.

sentences.zh: 先是，尚書祠部奏從博士張靖議，皇太子亦從制俱釋服。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Ministry of Rites had memorialized following Erudite Zhang Jing's opinion—the crown prince likewise followed regulation and together removed mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites had already accepted Zhang Jing's view, so the heir was told to strip hemp with everyone else.

sentences.zh: 博士陳逵議，以為「今制所依，蓋漢帝權制，興於有事，非禮之正。

translations.literal: Erudite Chen Kui held that 'the regulation we follow today is the Han emperor's expedient system, born of emergency—it is not orthodox ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kui argued the current rule was Han Wendi's wartime shortcut, not classical mourning.

sentences.zh: 皇太子無有國事，自宜終服。

translations.literal: The crown prince has no state business of his own—naturally he ought complete the full mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The heir had no throne duties; he should keep the full vigil.

sentences.zh: 」有詔更詳議。

translations.literal: ' There was an edict ordering further detailed debate.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' The throne ordered another round of discussion.'"

sentences.zh: 尚書杜預以為：「古者天子諸侯三年之喪始同齊斬，既葬除喪服，諒闇以居，心喪終制，不與士庶同禮。

translations.literal: Minister Du Yu held that 'in antiquity the Son of Heaven and feudal lords began three years' mourning alike in qi- and zhan-grade hemp; once burial ended they removed mourning garments, dwelt in silent seclusion (liang'an), and finished with heart mourning—not the same ritual as gentlemen and commoners.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said antiquity had sovereigns shed hemp at burial and finish mourning in seclusion, unlike commoners who wear weeds the whole term.

sentences.zh: 漢氏承秦，率天下為天子修服三年。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin and compelled all under Heaven to observe three years of mourning garments for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Han continued Qin's demand that the realm dress in mourning for the emperor three full years.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝見其下不可久行，而不知古制，更以意制祥禫，除喪即吉。

translations.literal: Han Wendi saw that his subordinates could not long sustain it, yet did not know the ancient system; further by his own intent fashioned xiang and dan rites, removed mourning, and went auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Wendi knew the bureaucracy could not bear three years of hemp yet misunderstood antiquity, so he invented xiang and dan and jumped back to court dress.

sentences.zh: 魏氏直以訖葬為節，嗣君皆不復諒闇終制。

translations.literal: The Wei house simply took the completion of burial as the limit—successive lords never again practiced silent seclusion to the end of the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sovereigns stopped mourning at interment and dropped the old liang'an vigil entirely.

sentences.zh: 學者非之久矣，然竟不推究經傳，考其行事，專謂王者三年之喪，當以衰麻終二十五月。

translations.literal: Scholars have faulted this a long time—yet in the end they did not investigate classics and commentary, examine actual practice, and solely assert that for kings three years' mourning ought mean wearing frayed hemp through twenty-five months.
translations.idiomatic: Critics have complained for generations yet never checked the texts: they insist the Son of Heaven must keep hemp twenty-five months.

sentences.zh: 嗣君苟若此，則天子群臣皆不得除喪。

translations.literal: If successor lords were like this, then the Son of Heaven and all ministers could never remove mourning.
translations.idiomatic: If every heir did that, neither throne nor bureaucracy could ever leave mourning.

sentences.zh: 雖志在居篤，更逼而不行。

translations.literal: Though their intent lay in dwelling earnestly, they were pressed and unable to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers meant to mourn deeply but circumstance made it impossible.

sentences.zh: 至今世主皆從漢文輕典，由處制者非制也。

translations.literal: Down to the present generation's lords all follow Han Wendi's light canon—because those who framed the system were not establishing true system.
translations.idiomatic: Every recent emperor still follows Wendi's thin code—because the framers never wrote real classical law.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子與尊同體，宜復古典，卒哭除衰麻，以諒闇終制。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince shares one body with the honored—he ought restore the ancient classic: at zuku remove frayed hemp, use silent seclusion to end the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The heir is ritually one with the sovereign and should return to the old path: shed hemp at wailing's end and complete mourning in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 于義既不應不除，又無取于漢文，乃所以篤喪禮也。

translations.literal: By right he neither ought refuse removal; nor is there reason to imitate Han Wendi—this thereby deepens the mourning ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: He must not cling to weeds, yet he need not copy Wendi either—this is how true mourning deepens.'

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書僕射盧欽、尚書魏舒問杜預證據所依。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon Vice Ministers Lu Qin and Wei Shu asked Du Yu what evidence he relied on.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' Lu Qin and Wei Shu then pressed Du Yu for his sources.'"

sentences.zh: 預云：「傳稱三年之喪自天子達，此謂天子絕期，唯有三年喪也。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'The commentary states that three years' mourning extends from the Son of Heaven downward—this means the Son of Heaven cuts off qi-grade mourning and only the three-year mourning [in heart] applies.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu answered that 'three years from the Son of Heaven down' means the ruler ends graded mourning while still owing the full inner term.

sentences.zh: 非謂居喪衰服三年，與士庶同也。

translations.literal: It does not mean dwelling in mourning garments and wearing frayed hemp for three years, the same as gentlemen and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: It does not mean twenty-five months in hemp like a common scholar.

sentences.zh: 故后、世子之喪，而叔向稱有三年之喪二也。

translations.literal: Therefore regarding the empress and crown prince's mourning, Shu Xiang spoke of there being two instances of 'three years' mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: That is why Shu Xiang could speak of two simultaneous three-year obligations for empress and heir.

sentences.zh: 周公不言高宗服喪三年，而云諒闇三年，此釋服心喪之文也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou did not say that Gaozong wore mourning garments three years, but said he 'dwelt in silence' three years—this is text explaining removing garments and observing heart mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents never say Gaozong wore weeds three years—only that he kept three years of hushed seclusion, which is the proof of garment removal with inner mourning.

sentences.zh: 叔向不譏景王除喪，而譏其燕樂已早，明既葬應除，而違諒闇之節也。

translations.literal: Shu Xiang did not reproach King Jing for removing mourning, but reproached his banquet music as too early—clarifying that once burial one ought remove mourning, yet he violated the moderation of silent seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Xiang faulted King Jing not for ending hemp but for piping too soon—burial ends dress mourning, not the quiet vigil.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，晉侯享諸侯，子產相鄭伯，時簡公未葬，請免喪以聽命，君子謂之得禮。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn, the Marquis of Jin feasted the feudal lords; Zichan assisted the Earl of Zheng—at the time Duke Jian was not yet buried—he requested to set aside mourning to hear commands—the gentlemen called this obtaining ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Jian of Zheng still lay unburied, Zichan asked leave to attend Jin's feast in court dress, and the Zuo judges called it proper.

sentences.zh: 宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵，傳曰『弔生不及哀』。

translations.literal: Steward Xuan came to present condolence gifts for Dukes Hui and Zhongzi; the commentary states 'condoling the living does not catch up with mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: The steward Xuan brought gifts for the living consorts while the lords were still unwailed, and the gloss says condolences to the living miss the funeral.

sentences.zh: 此皆既葬除服諒闇之證，先儒舊說，往往亦見，學者來之思耳。

translations.literal: These all are proofs of removing garments after burial and of silent seclusion—former Confucians' old explanations often appear as well—scholars simply have not pondered them.
translations.idiomatic: Each case shows hemp ends at burial and silence follows—older scholars noted it, but later readers ignored them.

sentences.zh: 《喪服》，諸侯為天子亦斬衰，豈可謂終服三年邪！

translations.literal: In Mourning Garments, feudal lords for the Son of Heaven likewise wear zhan-cui—how can one say they complete hemp garments for three years!
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments canon still has lords wear zhan-cui for the king—nobody keeps it three full years.

sentences.zh: 上考七代，未知王者君臣上下衰麻三年者誰；

translations.literal: Looking up through seven generations, I do not know which king's lord and minister, high and low, wore frayed hemp for three years;
translations.idiomatic: Scanning seven reigns backward, I find no sovereign and court who wore weeds the full span.

sentences.zh: 下推將來，恐百世之主其理一也。

translations.literal: projecting down to the future, I fear that for a hundred generations' lords the principle will be one.
translations.idiomatic: Project forward a hundred rulers and the logic will be the same.

sentences.zh: 非必不能，乃事勢不得，故知聖人不虛設不行之制。

translations.literal: It is not that they could not—it is that the momentum of affairs did not allow it—therefore know that sages do not vainly establish systems that cannot be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: They were not unwilling—circumstance forbade it—so the sages never wrote laws that no throne could live.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰『禮所損益雖百世可知』，此之謂也。

translations.literal: Zhongni said 'ritual's diminishing and increasing, though a hundred generations, can be known'—this is what is meant.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said ritual's wax and wane stays legible across ages—he meant exactly this.'

sentences.zh: 」於是飲、舒從之，遂命預造議，奏曰：

translations.literal: ' Thereupon Qin and Shu followed him; then they ordered Yu to draft a memorial, submitting:'
translations.idiomatic: ' Lu Qin and Wei Shu concurred and told Du Yu to formalize the argument in a memorial.'

sentences.zh: 於是太子遂以厭降之議，從國制除衰麻，諒闇終制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crown prince, by the debate on suppressive lowering, followed state regulation removing frayed hemp and used silent seclusion to end the mourning regulation.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis the heir shed hemp under the expedient code and finished mourning in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 于時外內卒聞預異議，多怪之。

translations.literal: At that time, inside and outside the court, upon hearing Yu's different opinion, most thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Court and camp alike thought Du Yu's view bizarre.

sentences.zh: 或者乃謂其違禮以合時。

translations.literal: Some even said he violated ritual to suit the times.
translations.idiomatic: Some accused him of bending the canon to please fashion.

sentences.zh: 時預亦不自解說，退使博士段暢博采典籍，為之證據，令大義著明，足以垂示將來。

translations.literal: At the time Yu also did not explain himself; he retired and ordered Erudite Duan Chang broadly to gather classics and canons as evidence for him, so that the great meaning would shine clearly and suffice to instruct posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said little himself but told Duan Chang to mine the classics for proofs that would settle the debate for later ages.

sentences.zh: 暢承預旨，遂撰集書傳舊文，條諸實事成言，以為定證，以弘指趣。

translations.literal: Chang received Yu's intent, then compiled transmitted old texts, itemizing verified events into sayings, as fixed proofs, to broaden the purport.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Chang collated precedents and tagged each with a gloss to anchor Du Yu's thesis.

sentences.zh: 其傳記有與今議同者，亦具列之，博舉二隅，明其會歸，以證斯事。

translations.literal: Wherever records agreed with today's debate, he likewise listed them in full—broadly raising two angles, clarifying their convergence, to prove this affair.
translations.idiomatic: He cited parallels that matched the new rule and mapped how they converged on one conclusion.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is extensive and is not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The compilation ran long and is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 武帝楊悼皇后既母養懷帝，后遇難時，懷帝尚幼，及即位，中詔述后恩愛。

translations.literal: Empress Yang Dao of Emperor Wu had already mother-nurtured Emperor Huai; when she later met violent death, Emperor Huai was still young; when he ascended, an inner edict recounted the empress's kindness and love.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang had raised the future Emperor Huai; when she was killed he was still a child, and on enthronement he issued a palace rescript praising her care.

sentences.zh: 及后祖載，群官議帝應為追制服，或以庶母慈己，依禮制小功五月，或以謂慈母服如母服齊衰者，眾議不同。

translations.literal: When later her funeral train departed, the many offices debated whether the emperor ought wear retroactive mourning—or some said because a concubine-mother had loved him, by ritual he should wear xiao gong five months—or some said foster-mother mourning like a mother's qi-cui—the many opinions differed.
translations.idiomatic: At her cortège the ministries split: some wanted retroactive weeds, some cited a nurturing concubine's xiao gong, some equated her to a legal mother in qi-cui.

sentences.zh: 閭丘沖議云：「楊后母養聖上，蓋以曲情。

translations.literal: Luqiu Chong debated: 'Empress Yang mother-nurtured the sage ascendant—generally out of special affection.'
translations.idiomatic: Luqiu Chong argued that Empress Yang had raised the sovereign with extraordinary devotion beyond the usual duty.

sentences.zh: 今以恩禮追崇，不配世祖廟。

translations.literal: Now by kindness and ritual we posthumously honor her—not pairing her in Emperor Shizu's temple.
translations.idiomatic: The court would exalt her by kindness yet not enshrine her beside Emperor Wu's tablet.

sentences.zh: 王者無慈養之服，謂宜祖載之日，可三朝素服發哀而已。

translations.literal: For kings there is no garment for 'foster nurturing'; I say on the day of the funeral train, three court sessions in plain dress to raise mourning is enough.'
translations.idiomatic: Kings have no canonical grade for a nurse; plain dress for three audiences at the hearse should suffice.

sentences.zh: 」於是從之。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon [the court] followed this.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' The throne accepted his view.'"

sentences.zh: 康帝正月晦，成恭杜皇后周忌，有司奏，至尊期年應改服。

translations.literal: On the last day of the first month under Emperor Kang fell the full-cycle anniversary of Empress Cheng-Gong née Du; the offices memorialized that the sovereign after one full year ought change garments.
translations.idiomatic: Kang's calendar hit Empress Du's first anniversary; officials asked him to switch out of deepest mourning.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「君親，名教之重也，權制出於近代耳。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'Lord and parent are what name-teaching esteems most heavily—expedient regulation arose only in recent generations.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered that ruler and father anchor ethics, while shortened mourning is a late invention.

sentences.zh: 」於是素服如舊，固非漢魏之典也。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon plain dress as before—indeed this is not Han-Wei canonical precedent.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' He kept plain dress anyway—far from Han or Wei orthodoxy.'"

sentences.zh: ，哀帝章皇太妃薨，帝欲服重。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] The Honored Consort Zhang of Emperor Ai died; the emperor wished to wear heavy mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ai's Honored Lady Zhang died, and he wanted the heaviest weeds.

sentences.zh: 江虨啟：「先王制禮，應在緦服。

translations.literal: Jiang Pin presented: 'The former kings' ritual system—ought to be si-grade hemp.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pin said the classics fixed only si-grade mourning for her.

sentences.zh: 」詔欲降期，虨又啟：「厭屈私情，所以上嚴祖考。

translations.literal: The edict wished to lower to qi [one full year]; Pin again presented: 'Suppressing and bending private feeling is thereby to give utmost respect to remote ancestors.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor pressed for qi-grade mourning, Jiang argued that curbing private grief exalts the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 」於是制緦麻三月。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the system fixed si hemp for three months.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' The court settled on three months of si hemp.'"

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康中，崇德太后褚氏崩。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's Ningkang era, Empress Dowager Chongde née Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: During Ningkang, Empress Dowager Chongde of the Chu clan died.

sentences.zh: 后於帝為從嫂，或疑其服。

translations.literal: Toward the emperor she was his elder brother's wife—some doubted the mourning grade.
translations.idiomatic: To the reigning emperor she was a sister-in-law, so ministers argued the garment.

sentences.zh: 博士徐藻議，以為：「資父事君而敬同。

translations.literal: Erudite Xu Zao debated, holding that 'nurturing a father and serving a lord share the same reverence.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zao said serving a foster father matches serving a lord in gravity.

sentences.zh: 又，禮，其夫屬父道者，其妻皆母道也。

translations.literal: Moreover by ritual: when a husband falls under the 'father's way,' his wives all fall under the 'mother's way.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites add that wives track their husband's ritual 'way' toward parents.

sentences.zh: 則夫屬君道，妻亦后道矣。

translations.literal: Then when the husband falls under the 'lord's way,' the wife likewise falls under the 'empress's way.'
translations.idiomatic: If the husband owes a lord's reverence, the wife owes an empress the same.

sentences.zh: 服后宜以資母之義。

translations.literal: For the empress dowager one ought by the meaning of a nurturing mother.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning her therefore follows the 'nurturing mother' rule.

sentences.zh: 魯譏逆祀，以明尊尊。

translations.literal: Lu reproached inverted sacrifice—to clarify honoring the honored.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu annals faulted misplaced sacrifice to keep rank clear.

sentences.zh: 今上躬奉康、穆、哀皇及靖后之祀，致敬同於所天。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign personally attends sacrifice to Emperors Kang, Mu, and Ai and to Empress Jing—pays utmost reverence the same as to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself offers to Kang, Mu, Ai, and Empress Jing with awe equal to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 豈可敬之以君道，而服廢於本親。

translations.literal: How can one reverence her by the lord's way yet in garments cast off close kin.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot treat her as a liege in cult yet deny her kinship in dress.

sentences.zh: 謂應服齊衰期。

translations.literal: I say he ought wear qi-cui for one full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zao prescribed qi-cui for one year.

sentences.zh: 」於是帝制期服。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the emperor regulated qi-grade mourning.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' The throne adopted qi-cui mourning.'"

sentences.zh: ，孝武太皇太后李氏崩，疑所服。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] Grand Empress Dowager Li of Xiaowu died—there was doubt about the garment.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Empress Dowager Li died, the court disputed the proper weeds.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射何澄、右僕射王雅、尚書車胤、孔安國、祠部郎徐廣議、太皇太后名位允正，體同皇極，理制備盡，情禮彌申。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister He Cheng, right Vice Minister Wang Ya, ministers Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang of the Ritual Section debated: the grand empress dowager's title and rank are correct—her body matches the supreme pole—principle and system are complete, feeling and ritual further extend.
translations.idiomatic: He Cheng, Wang Ya, Che Yin, Kong Anguo, and Xu Guang argued her title was orthodox, her station matched the pole, and both law and sentiment demanded full mourning.

sentences.zh: 《陽秋》之義，母以子貴，既稱夫人，禮服從正。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn meaning: the mother is honored through the son—once she is titled lady, ritual garments follow correctness.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo principle 'mother honored by son' means a titled consort takes the full garment schedule.

sentences.zh: 故成風顯夫人之號，文公服三年之喪。

translations.literal: Therefore Cheng Feng bore the lady's title; Duke Wen observed three years' mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Duke Wen wore three years for Lady Chengfeng once she was titled mother.

sentences.zh: 子于父之所生，體尊義重。

translations.literal: The son toward the parent who bore him—body venerable, meaning heavy.
translations.idiomatic: A son owes the birth parent both dignity and deep obligation.

sentences.zh: 且禮，祖不厭孫，固宜遂服無屈，而緣情立制。

translations.literal: Moreover by ritual the founding ancestor does not suppress the grandson—therefore it is fitting to follow the garment without bending, yet by feeling establish regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors do not override grandsons, so nothing in the canon forces a reduction, though feeling may shape the grade.

sentences.zh: 若嫌明文不存，則疑斯從重，謂應同于為祖母后齊衰期。

translations.literal: If one suspects the clear text does not survive, then in doubt follow the heavier—I say one ought match wearing qi-cui one cycle for a grandmother-empress.
translations.idiomatic: Where scripture is unclear, choose the heavier rule—here that means qi-cui for a grandmother-empress.

sentences.zh: 永安皇后無服，但一舉哀，百官亦一期。

translations.literal: Empress Yong'an had no garment—only once raised mourning; the hundred officials likewise one cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yong'an had worn no formal grade—only a single wail—yet ministers still observed one cycle for her.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: ' The edict approved.'"
translations.idiomatic: ' The rescript said yes.'"

sentences.zh: 孝武帝，淑媛陳氏卒，皇太子所生也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu—Honored Lady Chen died—she was the crown prince's birth mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Honored Lady Chen—mother of the heir—died under Xiaowu,

sentences.zh: 有司參詳母以子貴，贈淑媛為夫人，置家令典喪事。

translations.literal: The offices deliberated in detail: the mother is honored through the son—posthumously honored the Honored Lady as lady—established a household steward to manage funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the ministries invoked 'mother honored by son,' raised her to Lady, and assigned a household steward for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 太子前衛率徐邈議：「《喪服傳》稱與尊者為體，則不服其私親。

translations.literal: Former crown-prince guard commander Xu Miao debated: "The Mourning Garments Commentary states that when one forms one body with the honored person, then one does not wear mourning for one's private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao, lately commander of the crown prince's guard, cited the Mourning Garments subcommentary: whoever is ritually one with a superior does not observe mourning for a private parent.

sentences.zh: 又，君父所不服，子亦不敢服。

translations.literal: Moreover, what lord and father does not wear, the son likewise dare not wear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a son may not wear mourning that his sovereign father foregoes.

sentences.zh: 故王公妾子服其所生母練冠麻衣，既葬而除，非五服之常，則謂之無服。

translations.literal: Therefore royal lords' sons by concubines wear for their birth mothers lien cap and hemp cloth—once buried then remove—not among the five garments' constant norms—then it is called having no garment.
translations.idiomatic: Hence princes' sons by concubines wear only a plain lien cap and hemp until burial, then lay them aside—outside the five canonical grades—ritually counted as "no mourning."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court accepted his reading.

sentences.zh: ，孝武帝崩，孝武太后制三年之服。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Emperor Xiaowu died—Empress Dowager Xiaowu regulated three years' garments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, Empress Dowager Xiaowu ordered full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 惠帝三月，皇太孫尚薨。

translations.literal: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, the imperial grandson-heir Shang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Emperor Hui's reign, Sima Shang, heir as imperial grandson, died.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，御服齊衰期。

translations.literal: The offices memorialized that the sovereign should wear qi-cui for one full year (qi).
translations.idiomatic: The authorities asked that the emperor observe qi-cui mourning for the standard one-year term.

sentences.zh: 詔下通議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered general court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent down an edict for the whole bureaucracy to debate the matter.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍謝衡以為：「諸侯之太子，誓與未誓，尊卑體殊。

translations.literal: Cavalier attendant-in-ordinary Xie Heng held: "For a feudal lord's heir apparent, sworn presentation versus not yet sworn—the honored base and bodily tie differ.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Heng, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, argued that for a feudal heir's ritual standing, whether or not he had undergone the sworn presentation rite made a real difference in rank and ritual "one body."

sentences.zh: 《喪服》云為嫡子長殤，謂未誓也，已誓則不殤也。

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments [canon] states mourning for the eldest legitimate son's long shang means not yet sworn; once sworn then it is not [counted as] shang.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments canon treats mourning for an eldest legitimate son who dies in the "long shang" bracket as applying only before the sworn presentation; after that rite he is no longer classed as a shang death.

sentences.zh: 」中書令卞粹曰：「太子始生，故已尊重，不待命誓。

translations.literal: " Minister of the Secretariat Bian Cui said: "The heir apparent from birth is therefore already honored high—does not await mandate-swearing.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Cui, minister of the Secretariat, answered that a crown prince is already supreme in rank from birth and does not wait upon any separate mandate or sworn presentation.

sentences.zh: 若衡議已誓不殤，則無服之子當斬衰三年；

translations.literal: If by Xie's debate sworn means not shang, then the son for whom there is no [shang-scale] garment ought wear zhan-cui three years;
translations.idiomatic: If Xie's rule—sworn, therefore not shang—were accepted, any son outside the shang grades would require the mourner to wear zhan-cui for three full years;

sentences.zh: 未誓而殤，則雖十九當大功九月。

translations.literal: not sworn and [dies as] shang, then though age nineteen ought wear da gong nine months.
translations.idiomatic: yet if he had not been sworn and still counted as shang, even at nineteen the prescribed grade would be only da gong for nine months.

sentences.zh: 誓與未誓，其為升降也微；

translations.literal: Sworn and not sworn—the rise and fall therein is slight;
translations.idiomatic: The ritual gap between sworn and unsworn is tiny;

sentences.zh: 斬衰與大功，其為輕重也遠。

translations.literal: zhan-cui and da gong—the light and heavy therein is far apart.
translations.idiomatic: but the gulf between zhan-cui and da gong is enormous.

sentences.zh: 而今注云『諸侯不降嫡殤重』。

translations.literal: Yet now the commentary states 'feudal lords do not lower the weight of legitimate-son shang.'
translations.idiomatic: The gloss nonetheless says feudal lords do not mitigate mourning for a legitimate son who dies young.

sentences.zh: 嫌于無服，以大功為重嫡之服，則雖誓，無復有三年之理明矣。

translations.literal: Loath to [say] no garment, taking da gong as the garment weighting the legitimate heir—then though sworn, there is no longer principle for three years—this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid calling it "no mourning," commentators assign da gong as the heavy mourning for the heir—so even after the sworn rite, three years of zhan-cui simply cannot apply. That much is plain.

sentences.zh: 男能衛社稷，女能奉婦道，以可成之年而有已成之事，故可無殤，非孩齔之謂也。

translations.literal: When a male can guard altars of soil and grain and a female can uphold the wifely way—in years when completion is possible yet matters already accomplished—therefore may be without shang—it does not mean infant teeth.
translations.idiomatic: A lad old enough to defend the altars, or a girl able to discharge a wife's duties, has crossed out of the shang brackets once capable adulthood is acknowledged—not toddlers still at breast.

sentences.zh: 為殤後者尊之如父，猶無所加而止殤服，況以天子之尊，而為無服之殤行成人之制邪！

translations.literal: One who succeeds a shang [decedent] honors him like a father—still adds nothing and stops at shang garment—how much more with Heaven's Son's honor to enact adult norms for a shang without garment!
translations.idiomatic: An heir who continues a shang line honors the dead like a father yet still caps mourning at the shang grades—how then could the Son of Heaven impose full adult mourning where the canon prescribes none?

sentences.zh: 凡諸宜重之殤，皆士大夫不加服，而令至尊獨居其重，未之前聞也。

translations.literal: All shangs that ought be weighted—great officers add no garment—yet to make the supremacy alone bear the weight—never before heard.
translations.idiomatic: Every other heavy shang case lets ministers stop short of extra mourning; to load that weight solely onto the sovereign would be without precedent.

sentences.zh: 」博士蔡克同粹。

translations.literal: " Erudite Cai Ke agreed with Bian Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Court erudite Cai Ke sided with Bian Cui.

sentences.zh: 秘書監摯虞云：「太子初生，舉以成人之禮，則殤理除矣。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Library Zhi Yu said: "The heir apparent from birth is raised with adult rites—then shang principle is removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, director of the palace library, said the crown prince is invested from birth with ceremonies meant for adults, so the logic of "shang" mourning drops away entirely.

sentences.zh: 太孫亦體君傳重，由位成而服，全非以年也。

translations.literal: The grand heir likewise forms one body with the lord and transmits weight—garments follow from position achieved, wholly not by age.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson-heir likewise embodies the ruler and bears the ritual "weight"; mourning follows his station, not his calendar age.

sentences.zh: 天子無服殤之義，絕期故也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven has no principle of wearing [mourning for] shang—because [such ties] are cut off at one full cycle (qi).
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven never wears shang-grade mourning for kin, precisely because those relationships are ritually severed at the one-year boundary.

sentences.zh: 」於是從之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon [the court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted this view.

sentences.zh: 魏氏故事，國有大喪，群臣凶服，以帛為綬囊，以布為劍衣。

translations.literal: Wei-house precedent: when the state had great mourning, many ministers wore funeral dress—silk for seal-cord pouches, cloth for sword sheaths.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei dynasty usage, a dynastic funeral saw ministers in mourning garb with silk pouches for seal cords and cloth wrappers for swords.

sentences.zh: 新禮，以《傳》稱「去喪無所不佩」，明在喪則無佩也，更制齊斬之喪不佩劍綬。

translations.literal: The New Rites, because the Commentary states 'upon leaving mourning nothing is not suspended,' clarifies that in mourning there is no suspension—reformed so qi-cui and zhan-cui mourning do not suspend sword and seal cord.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin "New Rites" cited the gloss "after mourning ends, everything may hang from the belt" to infer that during mourning nothing should hang there, and barred sword and seal cord under qi-cui and zhan-cui.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為「《周禮》武賁氏，士大夫之職也，皆以兵守王宮，國有喪故，則衰葛執戈楯守門，葬則從車而哭。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held that "the Zhou Rites' Wu-ben guards—great officers' duty—all with arms guard the royal palace; when the state has mourning cause, then [wear] frayed robe and kudzu, grasp halberd and shield guarding gates; at burial then follow carts and wail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu countered that the Zhou Rites' royal guardsmen were officers under arms who defended the palace; on a national bereavement they wore mourning hemp with shield and polearm at the gates and followed the hearse wailing.

sentences.zh: 又，成王崩，太保命諸大夫以干戈內外警設。

translations.literal: Moreover, when King Cheng died, Grand Protect ordered various great officers with shields and halberds to set inner and outer vigil.
translations.idiomatic: When King Cheng died, the Grand Protect ordered ministers to stand watch inside and out with shields and halberds.

sentences.zh: 明喪故之際，蓋重宿衛之防。

translations.literal: This clarifies that at mourning's crisis one esteems night-watch defense.
translations.idiomatic: That shows how gravely a reign treats palace security even amid mourning.

sentences.zh: 去喪無所不佩，謂服飾之事，不謂防禦之用。

translations.literal: 'Upon leaving mourning nothing not suspended' speaks of adornment matters—not defense uses.
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing suspended after mourning" governs dress ornaments, not weapons of defense.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮布衣劍如舊，其餘如新制。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites: cloth garment and sword as of old—the rest as new regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites should keep cloth sword covers as before and leave the rest under the new rules.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，將葬，設吉凶鹵簿，皆以鼓吹。

translations.literal: Han-Wei precedent: nearing burial, set auspicious and inauspicious halberd-escort arrays—all used drum-and-pipe.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei practice paired auspicious and funeral halberd escorts at burial, both complete with military music.

sentences.zh: 新禮以禮無吉駕導從之文，臣子不宜釋其衰麻以服玄黃，除吉駕鹵簿。

translations.literal: The New Rites held the rites lack text for auspicious carriages with outriders—ministers and sons ought not shed their frayed hemp to wear black-and-yellow—removed auspicious-carriage halberd escort.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites argued classical texts never sanctioned festive carriages and outriders for a burial, so ministers should not strip mourning hemp for court blacks—and struck the auspicious half of the halberd escort.

sentences.zh: 又，凶事無樂，遏密八音，除凶服之鼓吹。

translations.literal: Moreover, inauspicious affairs have no music—suppress and silence the eight tones—removed drum-and-pipe from funeral dress [processions].
translations.idiomatic: Funerals should silence every instrument, they added, so drum-and-pipe bands had to go from the mourning procession as well.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「葬有祥車曠左，則今之容車也。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Burial has auspicious cart with empty left seat—that is today's appearance cart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu replied that the classic "auspicious cart with the left seat left empty" is the ancestor of today's display carriage.

sentences.zh: 既葬，日中反虞，逆神而還。

translations.literal: Once buried, at midday perform returning yu, welcome the spirit back.
translations.idiomatic: After interment, the noon returning-yu rite escorts the spirit home again.

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》，鄭大夫公孫蠆卒，天子追賜大路，使以行。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Commentary: Zheng grand officer Gongsun Chai died—the Son of Heaven posthumously granted great road-chariot, ordering it used for the procession.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition records how, when Zheng minister Gongsun Chai died, the Zhou king sent a state chariot so the cortège could ride in due splendor.

sentences.zh: 《士喪禮》，葬有稿車乘車，以載生之服。

translations.literal: The Gentlemen's Mourning Rites: burial has straw cart and riding cart—to carry garb [used] in life.
translations.idiomatic: The "Gentleman's Mourning" specifies straw carts and riding carts bearing the clothes the dead wore in life.

sentences.zh: 此皆不唯載柩，兼有吉駕之明文也。

translations.literal: These all not only bear the coffin—together they have explicit text for auspicious carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Those provisions plainly sanction festive vehicles alongside the bier, not coffins alone.

sentences.zh: 既設吉駕，則宜有導從，以象平生之容，明不致死之義。

translations.literal: Once auspicious carriages are set, then fittingly there should be outriders—to image deportment in life, clarifying the meaning of not treating [the deceased] as utterly dead.
translations.idiomatic: Where such carriages appear, outriders belong too—the ritual echoes how the noble lived and insists he is not cast away like carrion.

sentences.zh: 臣子衰麻不得為身而釋，以為君父則無不可。
