translations.literal: Ministers and sons in frayed hemp may not for themselves shed—for lord and father then nothing impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: A minister may not shrug off mourning for private convenience, yet for his lord or father nothing in the canon forbids fitting splendor to the cortège.

sentences.zh: 《顧命》之篇足以明之。

translations.literal: The 'Charge at Gu' piece suffices to clarify this.
translations.idiomatic: The "Charge at Gu" chapter of the Documents proves the point.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮設吉服導從如舊，其凶服鼓吹宜除。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites to set auspicious-garment outriders as of old—the funeral drum-and-pipe ought be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu urged restoring festive outriders under the New Rites while still banning martial music on the mourning train.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事，大喪及大臣之喪，執紼者輓歌。

translations.literal: Han-Wei precedent: great mourning and great ministers' mourning—those holding tow-ropes sang dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei custom had catafalque bearers chant pulling-dirges at imperial funerals and at those of great ministers.

sentences.zh: 新禮以為輓歌出於漢武帝役人之勞歌，聲哀切，遂以為送終之禮。

translations.literal: The New Rites held dirges arose from Han Emperor Wu's corvée people's labor songs—sound mournful and piercing—thereupon taken as seeing-off-the-end rite.
translations.idiomatic: The New Rites traced those laments to corvée labor songs under Emperor Wu—voices sharp with grief—and showed how they had hardened into funeral practice.

sentences.zh: 雖音曲摧愴，非經典所制，違禮設銜枚之義。

translations.literal: Though melody is crushing-grief—not fashioned by classics—contravenes the rites' meaning of mouth-plugs.
translations.idiomatic: However wrenching the tunes, they are nowhere mandated in the classics and violate the spirit of biting wooden gag-bits to keep silence.

sentences.zh: 方在號慕，不宜以歌為名。

translations.literal: Just now in wailing longing—not fitting to take 'song' as name.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-wail for the dead, nothing should parade under the label of "song."

sentences.zh: 除，不輓歌。

translations.literal: Removed—no dirges.
translations.idiomatic: The reform abolished pulling-dirges altogether.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「輓歌因倡和而為摧愴之聲，銜枚所以全哀，此亦以感眾。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Dirges through lead-and-chorus become crushing sounds—mouth-plugs thereby preserve mourning—this too thereby moves the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu argued that antiphonal dirges shape communal grief, much as gag-bits enforce solemn silence—they stir the throng rather than cheapen it.

sentences.zh: 雖非經典所載，是歷代故事。

translations.literal: Though not carried in classics—it is successive dynasties' precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They never appear verbatim in the canon, yet dynasty after dynasty relied on them.

sentences.zh: 《詩》稱『君子作歌，惟以告哀』，以歌為名，亦無所嫌。

translations.literal: The Odes state 'the gentleman makes song—only to declare grief'—to take song as name—also nothing blameworthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes themselves praise the gentleman who "raises a song only to voice sorrow," so the word "song" is hardly improper.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮如舊。

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix the New Rites as of old.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the New Rites reinstate the older practice.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his opinion.

sentences.zh: ，安平穆王薨，無嗣，以母弟敦上繼獻王後，移太常問應何服。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Prince Mu of Anping died—no heir—his uterine younger brother Dun was elevated to continue Prince Xian's line—the case was referred to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials asking what mourning ought apply.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Mu of Anping died without issue, his full brother Sima Dun was promoted to continue Prince Xian's line; the matter went to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials to settle the proper mourning grades.

sentences.zh: 博士張靖答，宜依魯僖服閔三年例。

translations.literal: Erudite Zhang Jing replied—it should follow Duke Xi of Lu's mourning Duke Min three-year precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Zhang Jing answered that the parallel was Duke Xi of Lu wearing three years' mourning for Duke Min.

sentences.zh: 尚書符詰靖：「穆王不臣敦，敦不繼穆，與閔僖不同。

translations.literal: The Secretariat issued a writ pressing Jing: "Prince Mu did not treat Dun as subject—Dun does not succeed Mu—this differs from Min and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat shot back: Prince Mu never treated Dun as his subject, and Dun was not succeeding Prince Mu himself—nothing like the Duke Min and Duke Xi case.

sentences.zh: 」孫毓、宋昌議，以穆王不之國，敦不仕諸侯，不應三年。

translations.literal: " Sun Yu and Song Chang debated that because Prince Mu never went to his fief and Dun never served feudal lords, three years should not apply.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu and Song Chang countered that because Prince Mu never took up his fief and Dun had never served as a feudal officer, full three-year mourning was out of the question.

sentences.zh: 以義處之，敦宜服本服，一期而除，主穆王喪祭三年畢，乃吉祭獻王。

translations.literal: Judging by right principle, Dun ought wear his proper garment—remove after one full cycle (qi)—preside over Prince Mu's mourning sacrifices completing three years—then perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian.
translations.idiomatic: On principle, Dun should wear only his own proper grade—doffing it after the one-year term—yet still oversee Prince Mu's mortuary rites through three years before he may offer auspicious sacrifices to Prince Xian.

sentences.zh: 毓云：「《禮》，君之子孫所以臣諸兄者，以臨國故也。

translations.literal: Sun Yu said: "By the Rites, why lord's descendants treat elder brothers as lord—because they face the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yu cited the canon: princes' sons honor elder brothers as lords only when they actually rule a state.

sentences.zh: 《禮》又與諸侯為兄弟服斬者，謂鄰國之臣於鄰國之君，有猶君之義故也。

translations.literal: The Rites moreover [say] wearing zhan-cui for feudal-lord brothers means neighboring state's ministers toward neighboring state's lord—because there is quasi-lord meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan-cui for a brother who is another state's ruler applies only where ministers owe their neighbor's prince something like fealty.

sentences.zh: 今穆王既不之國，不臣兄弟，敦不仕諸侯，無鄰臣之義，異于閔僖，如符旨也。

translations.literal: Now Prince Mu neither went to state nor treated brothers as subjects—Dun never served feudal lords—no neighboring-minister meaning—differs from Min and Xi—as the writ's intent [states].
translations.idiomatic: Here Prince Mu never took his throne in the fief, never treated brothers as vassals, and Dun was no feudal minister—so none of the "neighbor's minister" logic applies, exactly as the Secretariat argued.

sentences.zh: 但喪無主，敦既奉詔紹國，受重主喪，典其祭祀。

translations.literal: But mourning lacked a master—Dun having received edict to continue the state—received weight and presided mourning—administers its sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the bereavement had no ritual head; Dun, ordered to continue the line, carries the "weight" of heirship, directs the funeral, and manages the offerings.

sentences.zh: 『大功者主人之喪，有三年者則必為之再祭』。

translations.literal: 'For da gong [mourning] the master's mourning—if there is one with three years then must perform for him twice the sacrifice.'
translations.idiomatic: "When the chief mourner wears da gong but someone else in the household still owes three full years, he must conduct both intermediate auspicious rites for them."

sentences.zh: 鄭氏《注》云，『謂死者之從父昆弟來為喪主也。

translations.literal: Zheng's Commentary states: '[This] means the deceased's father's brothers' sons who come as mourning master.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan glosses this as paternal cousins who arrive to act as funeral master.

sentences.zh: 」有三年者，謂妻若子幼少也』。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior quotation;] 'those who have three years' refers to wife or young children (close of Zheng Xuan gloss).
translations.idiomatic: Zheng finishes the gloss: the survivors who still owe three years are the widow or very young children.

sentences.zh: 『再祭，謂大小祥也』。

translations.literal: 'Twice sacrifice means great and small xiang.'
translations.idiomatic: "The two offerings are the great and small xiang rites."

sentences.zh: 穆妃及國臣於禮皆當三年，此為有三年者，敦當為之主大小兩祥祭也。

translations.literal: Prince Mu's consort and state ministers by rites all ought three years—these are those with three years—Dun ought for them preside both great- and small-xiang sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu's consort and his household ministers each owe three years of mourning; they are the "three-year" parties for whom Dun must preside over both xiang ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 且哀樂不相雜，吉凶不相干。

translations.literal: Moreover grief and joy do not mix—inauspicious and auspicious do not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover grief must not mingle with celebration, nor mourning with felicity.

sentences.zh: 凶服在宮，哭泣未絕。

translations.literal: Funeral dress in the palace—wailing not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral weeds still fill the palace and wails have not fallen silent.

sentences.zh: 敦遽主穆王之喪，而國制未除，則不得以己本親服除而吉祭獻王也。」

translations.literal: Dun hastily presides Prince Mu's mourning—yet state regulation not removed—then may not with his own kin garment removed perform auspicious sacrifice to Prince Xian."
translations.idiomatic: While Dun is abruptly directing Prince Mu's obsequies and the prescribed mourning is unfinished, he cannot shed mourning for his natural kin and turn to auspicious rites for Prince Xian."

sentences.zh: ，陳留國上，燕公是王之父，王出奉明帝祀，今于王為從父，有司奏應服期，不以親疏尊卑為降。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chenliu state reported—the Duke of Yan is the king's father—the king went out to serve Emperor Ming's sacrifices—now toward the king [the duke] is congfu kin—the offices memorialized [the duke] ought wear qi (one full cycle) mourning—not lowering by kin distance or honor base.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu memorialized that the Duke of Yan was the king's natural father; once the king had been given to continue Emperor Ming's line, the duke counted only as a congfu relative. Officials proposed qi-grade mourning with no reduction for intimacy or rank.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「王奉魏氏，所承者重，不得服其私親。

translations.literal: Edict stated: "The king carries Wei house—the inheritance is weighty—may not wear for private kin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict refused: "The king upholds Wei ancestry under grave obligation; he cannot observe mourning for a private parent."

sentences.zh: 」穆帝時，東海國言，哀王薨逾年，嗣王乃來繼，不復追服，群臣皆已反吉，國妃亦宜同除。

translations.literal: " Under Emperor Mu, Donghai state reported—King Ai died over a year—then the successor king came to continue—did not retroactively wear mourning—all ministers already returned auspicious—the state's royal consort likewise ought remove together.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Emperor Mu, Donghai argued that King Ai had been dead more than a year before the heir arrived, so no retroactive mourning was worn; ministers had all returned to felicity garb, and the princess-consort should shed weeds as well.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朝廷所以從權制者，以王事奪之，非為變禮也。

translations.literal: Edict stated: "Why the court followed expedient regulation—because royal affairs seized them—not to alter the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered: "We shortened mourning only because state business overrode private duty—not to rewrite the canon."

sentences.zh: 婦人傳重義大，若從權制，義將安托！

translations.literal: Women's transmitting weight—right meaning is great—if following expedient regulation—where will right rest!
translations.idiomatic: Women who bear the ritual "weight" of heirship hold immense obligation—if we subject them to the same expedient, where does principle find footing?

sentences.zh: 」於是國妃終三年之禮。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the state's royal consort completed three years' rites.
translations.idiomatic: The princess-consort therefore observed the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 孫盛以為：「廢三年之禮，開偷薄之源，漢魏失之大者也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng held: "Abolishing three years' rites—opens source of stingy thinness—Han-Wei's great failure.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng thought waiving three-year mourning opened the floodgates to meanness—that was Han and Wei's gravest ritual lapse.

sentences.zh: 今若以大夫宜奪以王事。

translations.literal: Now if holding great officers ought be seized by royal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If we allow that grandees may be yanked from mourning by state business,

sentences.zh: 婦人可終本服，是吉凶之儀雜陳于宮寢，彩素之制乖異於內外，無乃情禮俱違，哀樂失所乎！」

translations.literal: women may complete proper garment—is this not auspicious and inauspicious observances mixed in palace chambers—bright and plain regulations contrary inner and outer—surely emotion and rites both violated—grief and joy lose their place!"
translations.idiomatic: yet women finish full mourning for kin, would we not parade mourning and felicity through the same inner chambers, clash bright dress with hemp inside and out, and undo both feeling and ritual until grief and joy lose their proper seats?"

sentences.zh: ，太常車胤上言：「謹案《喪服禮經》，庶子為母緦麻三月。

translations.literal: [Text joins prior clause;] Chamberlain for Ceremonials Che Yin submitted: "Respectfully reviewing the Mourning Garments ritual classic—a son by concubine for mother [wears] si (fine hemp) three months.
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin, chamberlain for ceremonials, cited the Mourning Garments classic: a concubine's son owes his mother only three months in si-grade hemp.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『何以緦麻？

translations.literal: The Commentary states: 'Why si?
translations.idiomatic: The subcommentary asks why si applies.

sentences.zh: 以尊者為體，不敢服其私親也。

translations.literal: Because one forms body with the honored—dare not wear for private kin.
translations.idiomatic: Because the heir is ritually one with his exalted father, he cannot wear heavy mourning for a private parent.

sentences.zh: 』此《經》《傳》之明文，聖賢之格言。

translations.literal: ' This is classic and commentary's clear text—sages' model words.
translations.idiomatic: That pairing of text and gloss is explicit scripture—language the sages meant as normative.

sentences.zh: 而自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後，各肆私情，服其庶母，同之於嫡。

translations.literal: Yet from recently enfeoffed dukes and marquises down to ministers—sons by concubine who became heirs—each indulged private feeling—wore mourning for concubine-mothers—equating to legitimate mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately every enfeoffed noble down to senior ministers, once a concubine's son succeeded, indulged private affection and mourned a concubine-mother like a legal parent.

sentences.zh: 此末俗之弊，溺情傷教，縱而不革，則流遁忘返矣。

translations.literal: This is late custom's harm—drowning feeling injures teaching—if indulged and not reformed—then drift astray unable return.
translations.idiomatic: That late-born abuse drowns sentiment and wounds instruction; left unchecked, custom slides past recall.

sentences.zh: 且夫尊尊親親，雖禮之大本，然厭親于尊，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Moreover honoring honor and kinning kin—though rites' great root—yet subordinating kin to honor—from antiquity esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring superiors and cherishing kin are the roots of ritual, yet subordinating private kin to public rank has been honored since high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰，『為父後，出母無服也者，不祭故也』。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites states: 'Acting as father's heir—divorced mother no garment—because [one does] not sacrifice [to her] thereby.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says an heir to his father wears nothing for a divorced mother because he no longer sacrifices to her.

sentences.zh: 又，禮，天子父母之喪，未葬，越紼而祭天地社稷。

translations.literal: Moreover, by rites—Son of Heaven's father-mother mourning—not yet buried—step over rope-coffin and sacrifice to Heaven Earth soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Again, the Son of Heaven may vault the burial cord before interment and still offer to Heaven, Earth, and the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 斯皆崇嚴至敬，不敢以私廢尊也。

translations.literal: These all exalt stern utmost reverence—dare not with private discard honor.
translations.idiomatic: Such acts exalt awe before public cult—never letting private grief scrap obligations to the supreme powers.

sentences.zh: 今身承祖宗之重，而以庶母之私，廢烝嘗之事。

translations.literal: Now personally bearing ancestors' weight—yet with concubine-mother's private—abolish zheng-offering and chang-offering affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Today heirs shoulder ancestral temples yet scrap winter and autumn offerings for a concubine mother's sake.

sentences.zh: 五廟闕祀，由一妾之終，求之情禮，失莫大焉。

translations.literal: Five temples lack sacrifice—because one concubine's end—seek in emotion and rites—failure none greater.
translations.idiomatic: Five shrines miss sacrifice because one concubine died—by any measure of feeling or ritual, the harm could hardly be worse.

sentences.zh: 舉世皆然，莫之裁貶。

translations.literal: Whole age thus—none trims or faults it.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone does it; nobody reins it in.

sentences.zh: 就心不同，而事不敢異。

translations.literal: In heart disagree—but in deed dare not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Men may dissent inwardly yet dare not break step in public.

sentences.zh: 故正禮遂穨，而習非成俗。

translations.literal: Hence correct rites thus crumble—and habit wrong becomes custom.
translations.idiomatic: Thus orthodox ritual collapses while repeated error hardens into custom.

sentences.zh: 此《國風》所以思古，《小雅》所以悲歎。

translations.literal: This is why Airs of the States longs for antiquity—why Lesser Odes laments.
translations.idiomatic: This is why the Airs of the States sigh for ancient ways and the Lesser Odes pour out their grief.

sentences.zh: 當今九服漸甯，王化惟新，誠宜崇明禮訓，以一風俗。

translations.literal: Now the nine domains gradually pacified—kingly transformation anew—truly fitting exalt bright ritual instruction—to unify customs.
translations.idiomatic: With the nine circuits calming and royal influence renewing, it is time to lift bright ritual teaching and knit the realm into one custom.

sentences.zh: 請臺省考修經典，式明王度。

translations.literal: Request terrace and provincial offices examine and revise classics—to pattern-clarify kingly measure.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the central departments to collate the classics and codify them so the kingly norm shines clear.

sentences.zh: 」不答。

translations.literal: [Closing the edict;] there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne let the matter drop without answering.

sentences.zh: 十八年，胤又上言：「去年上，自頃開國公侯，至於卿士，庶子為後者，服其庶母，同之於嫡，違禮犯制，宜加裁抑。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Che Yin again memorialized: "Since last year's memorial, from recently enfeoffed dukes and marquises down to senior ministers, heirs born of concubines have worn mourning for concubine-mothers equal to a legal parent—this breaches ritual and statute and ought to be curbed."
translations.idiomatic: Che Yin renewed his plea: every new noble house, high or low, was mourning concubine-mothers like legal mothers, and the practice had to be checked.

sentences.zh: 事上經年，未被告報，未審朝議以何為疑。

translations.literal: The matter has been on high a full year without returned report—I do not know what doubt the court's deliberation still harbors.
translations.idiomatic: A year had passed with no answer, and he asked what in the court's mind still hesitated.

sentences.zh: 若以所陳或謬，則經有文；

translations.literal: If what I stated is mistaken, then the classics still contain explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: If his facts were wrong, the canon still spoke plainly.

sentences.zh: 若以古今不同，則晉有成典。

translations.literal: If ancient and modern differ, then Jin itself already has established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: If times had changed, Jin's own precedents settled the point.

sentences.zh: 升平四年，故太宰武陵王所生母喪，表求齊衰三年，詔聽依昔樂安王故事，制大功九月。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shengping, when the late grand preceptor the Prince of Wuling lost his birth mother, he asked for qi-cui three years; an edict allowed him to follow the former Prince of Le'an precedent and fixed da gong nine months.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Xi lost his natural mother in 360, he begged three years' mourning; the court granted the old Le'an prince compromise of nine months in da gong.

sentences.zh: ，故梁王㻱又所生母喪，亦求三年。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] When the late Prince of Liang Zhen likewise lost his birth mother, he again requested three years.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhen of Liang later asked for the same three-year favor for his concubine-born mother.

sentences.zh: 《庚子詔書》依太宰故事，同服大功。

translations.literal: The Gengzi edict followed the grand preceptor precedent and likewise prescribed da gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengzi palace rescript copied the grand preceptor's da gong rule.

sentences.zh: 若謹案周禮，則緦麻三月；

translations.literal: If one consults the Zhou Rites, the grade is si hemp for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou canon prescribes only three months in fine si hemp.

sentences.zh: 若奉晉制，則大功九月。

translations.literal: If one follows Jin statute, it is da gong for nine months.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's code points to nine months of da gong.

sentences.zh: 古禮今制，並無居廬三年之文，而頃年已來，各申私情，更相擬襲，漸以成俗。

translations.literal: Neither old rite nor current law ever authorized three years in the mourning hut—yet lately each house pleads private feeling and copies the next until it has hardened into custom.
translations.idiomatic: No classical text allows three years in weeds for this case, yet families keep imitating one another.

sentences.zh: 縱而不禁，則聖典滅矣。

translations.literal: If indulged and never forbidden, the sage canons are undone.
translations.idiomatic: Leave it unchecked and the canonical mourning system collapses.

sentences.zh: 夫尊尊親親，立人之本，王化所由，二端而已。

translations.literal: Honoring superiors and cherishing kin are the twin roots of becoming human; kingly transformation flows from these two channels alone.
translations.idiomatic: Revering rank and loving kin are what make a person human, and royal instruction rides on both.

sentences.zh: 故先王設教，務弘其極，尊郊社之敬，制越紼之禮，嚴宗廟之祀，厭庶子之服，所以經緯人文，化成天下。

translations.literal: Therefore former kings framed instruction to carry each principle to its height: they magnified suburban-altar awe, regulated the rite of vaulting the burial cord, tightened ancestral sacrifice, and suppressed mourning for concubine-mothers—by these they ordered civilization and transformed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients balanced heaven worship, tomb ritual, temple cult, and concubine sons so public duty could shape private life.

sentences.zh: 夫屈家事于王道，厭私恩於祖宗，豈非上行乎下，父行乎子！

translations.literal: Bending household duty to the kingly way and subordinating private grace to the ancestors—is this not the sovereign setting the pattern below and fathers doing the same for sons?
translations.idiomatic: State law was meant to pull kin feeling into line with the altars.

sentences.zh: 若尊尊之心有時而替，宜厭之情觸事而申，祖宗之敬微，而君臣之禮虧矣。

translations.literal: If reverence for rank ever falters and the feeling that ought to be suppressed surges at every turn, respect for ancestors thins and the rite between lord and minister collapses.
translations.idiomatic: Once rank yields to whim, ancestral awe and fealty both erode.

sentences.zh: 嚴恪微於祖宗，致敬虧於事上，而欲俗安化隆，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: When awe before ancestors grows slight and reverence toward superiors fails, expecting customs to mend and transformation to flourish—is that not difficult!
translations.idiomatic: You cannot starve the temples and court of respect yet expect the age to improve.

sentences.zh: 區區所惜，實在於斯。

translations.literal: What your humble servant cherishes lies precisely here.
translations.idiomatic: That is the heart of Che Yin's worry.

sentences.zh: 職之所司，不敢不言。

translations.literal: What my office oversees—I dare not keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: His portfolio obliged him to speak.

sentences.zh: 請臺參詳。

translations.literal: I ask the central departments to deliberate in detail."
translations.idiomatic: He begged the ministries to settle the rule in writing.'"

sentences.zh: 」尚書奏：「案如辭輒下主者詳尋。

translations.literal: The Ministry memorialized: "As the wording states, send it down to the supervisor to investigate in detail."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works returned the file for a full staff review.'"

sentences.zh: 依禮，庶子與尊者為體，不敢服其私親，此尊祖敬宗之義。

translations.literal: By ritual a son by concubine who is ritually one with the exalted may not wear mourning for a private parent—this is the meaning of revering ancestors and respecting the lineage."
translations.idiomatic: The canon bars an heir from heavy weeds for a concubine-mother when he embodies the succession—that is how ancestors stay supreme.'"

sentences.zh: 自頃陵遲，斯禮遂廢。

translations.literal: From recent decline this rite has been cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Lately men simply ignored it.

sentences.zh: 封國之君廢五廟之重，士庶匹夫闕烝嘗之禮，習成穨俗，宜被革正。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed lords toss away the weight of five shrines; gentlemen and commoners skip winter and autumn offerings—habit has slid into decay and ought to be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Princes neglect five-temple sacrifice, commoners skip seasonal offerings—custom needs a hard reset.

sentences.zh: 輒內外參詳，謂宜聽胤所上，可依樂安王大功為正。

translations.literal: We inner and outer offices have deliberated in detail and deem it fitting to accept what Yin submitted: take the Prince of Le'an's da gong as the correct standard."
translations.idiomatic: After joint review they endorsed Che Yin and made Le'an's da gong the binding precedent.'"

sentences.zh: 請為告書如左，班下內外，以定永制，普令依承，事可奉行。

translations.literal: Request that a proclamation be drafted as below, circulated inside and outside, to fix a perpetual rule so all may comply—the measure can then be enforced."
translations.idiomatic: They asked for an edict in fixed wording, promulgated empire-wide, to end the quarrel.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved."
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.'"

sentences.zh: 《禮》，王為三公六卿錫衰，為大夫士疑衰，首服弁絰。

translations.literal: The Rites prescribe that the king wears xi-cui for the Three Dukes and six ministers, yi-cui for great officers and gentlemen, with cap-band and zhui cord.
translations.idiomatic: Sovereigns don xi-cui for top ministers, yi-cui for lower ranks, capped with mourning ties.

sentences.zh: 天子諸侯皆為貴臣貴妾服三月。

translations.literal: Son of Heaven and feudal lords alike observe three months for honored ministers and honored concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers mourn favorite ministers and concubines three months by the same rule.

sentences.zh: 漢為大臣制服無聞焉。

translations.literal: I have not heard that Han prescribed mourning garments for great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Han sources never spell out court weeds for ministers.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時，東海恭王薨，帝出幸津門亭發哀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Han mourned the Prince Gong of Donghai, the sovereign went out to Jinmen pavilion to raise the lament.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mingdi rode to Jinmen kiosk to wail for his brother.

sentences.zh: 及武帝十一月，詔「諸王公大臣薨，應三朝發哀者，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀者，三日不舉樂也」。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wu in the eleventh month an edict read: "When princes, dukes, or great ministers die, those who owe three audiences of mourning shall have no music for over a month; those who owe one audience shall have no music for three days."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan's edict tied the length of musical silence to whether the court held one or three mourning audiences.

sentences.zh: 元帝姨廣昌鄉君喪，未葬，中丞熊遠表云：「案《禮》『君于卿大夫，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』，惻隱之心未忍行吉事故也。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan's maternal aunt the Lady of Guangchang village died, before burial Palace Secretary Xiong Yuan memorialized: "The Rites say the lord toward ministers and great officers—before burial does not eat meat, before the end of wailing does not raise music—because pitying hearts cannot yet bear auspicious business."
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan cited the canon to block court music while Yuan's aunt still lay unburied.

sentences.zh: 被尚書符，冬至後二日小會。

translations.literal: A Secretariat directive scheduled a small court gathering two days after the winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat still called a minor levee right after solstice.

sentences.zh: 臣以為廣昌鄉君喪殯日，聖恩垂悼。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that on the Lady of Guangchang's encoffining day sagely grace should show condolence.
translations.idiomatic: He asked the court to honor the burial with silence instead.

sentences.zh: 禮，大夫死，廢一時之祭。

translations.literal: By ritual, when a great officer dies, one season's sacrifice is suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The Mourning Garments rule pauses one seasonal offering when a senior minister dies.

sentences.zh: 祭猶可廢，而況餘事。

translations.literal: If sacrifice may be suspended, how much more other affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If even the altars may pause, lesser gatherings can wait.

sentences.zh: 冬至唯可群下奉賀而已，未便小會。

translations.literal: Winter solstice may only be an occasion for subordinates to offer congratulations—it is not yet fitting to convene a small assembly."
translations.idiomatic: The solstice levee should be congratulations only, not a banquet.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔以遠表示賀循，又曰：「武皇帝故事云『王公大臣薨，三朝發哀，逾月不舉樂，其一朝發哀，三日不舉樂』，此舊事明文。

translations.literal: The edict forwarded Xiong's statement to He Xun and added: "Emperor Wu's precedent reads: 'When princes, dukes, or great ministers die—three audiences of mourning, then no music for over a month; one audience, then no music for three days'—that old text is explicit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bounced the memo to He Xun and quoted Sima Yan's older edict verbatim.'"

sentences.zh: 」賀循答曰：「案《禮·雜記》，『君于卿大夫之喪，比葬不食肉，比卒哭不舉樂』。

translations.literal: He Xun replied: "Reviewing the Rites, Miscellaneous Records: 'The lord toward a minister's or great officer's mourning—before burial does not eat meat, before the end of wailing does not raise music.'"
translations.idiomatic: He Xun answered with the Zuo-era Miscellaneous Rites passage on abstaining from meat and music.'"

sentences.zh: 古者君臣義重，雖以至尊之義，降而無服，三月之內，猶錫衰以居，不接吉事。

translations.literal: In antiquity the bond between lord and minister was weighty: though the utmost honoring rites lowered the sovereign so he wore no full mourning, within three months he still dwelt in xi-cui and undertook no auspicious affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the crown wore only light weeds, the court still shunned feasts for three months.

sentences.zh: 故春秋晉大夫智悼子未葬，平公作樂，為屠蒯所譏。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn records that while Jin minister Zhi Ying lay unburied, Duke Ping ordered music and was rebuked by the blind musician Tu Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo narrative faulted Duke Ping of Jin for piping while Zhi Ying's bier was still above ground.

sentences.zh: 如遠所答，合于古義。

translations.literal: Xiong Yuan's answer matches ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Yuan had classical precedent on his side.

sentences.zh: 咸寧詔書雖不會經典，然隨時立宜，以為定制，誠非群下所得稱論。

translations.literal: The Xianning edict may not tally with every classic, yet it set workable law for its day and became fixed statute—not something subordinates should reopen at will."
translations.idiomatic: He Xun admitted the Xianning rescript was pragmatic, not scholastic, and should stand.'"

sentences.zh: 」，帝姑廬陵公主未葬，符問太常，冬至小會應作樂不。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] The emperor's paternal aunt the Princess of Luling was not yet buried when a writ asked the Chamberlain for Ceremonials whether the winter-solstice small assembly should use music.
translations.idiomatic: While Princess Luling still awaited burial, the ministry asked if the solstice dinner might have an orchestra.'"

sentences.zh: 博士胡訥議云：「君于卿大夫，比卒哭不舉樂。

translations.literal: Erudite Hu Na argued: "The lord toward ministers and great officers does not raise music before the end of wailing."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Na said music must wait until wailing finished.'"

sentences.zh: 公主有骨肉之親，宜闕樂。

translations.literal: The princess shares flesh-and-bone closeness—music ought to be omitted."
translations.idiomatic: A princess deserved the same musical silence.'"

sentences.zh: 」太常王彪之云：「案武帝詔，三朝舉哀，三旬乃舉樂；

translations.literal: Chamberlain Wang Bianzhi said: "Reviewing Emperor Wu's edict—three audiences of mourning, then music only after three decad-days;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bianzhi countered with Sima Yan's timetable: three audiences meant thirty days mute.'"

sentences.zh: 其一朝舉哀者，三日則舉樂。

translations.literal: those who hold one audience of mourning may raise music after three days."
translations.idiomatic: A single audience shortened the silence to three days.'"

sentences.zh: 春，長樂長公主薨，秋，扶風王駿薨，武帝並舉哀三日而已。

translations.literal: In spring the chief princess of Changle died; in autumn Prince Jun of Fufeng died—Emperor Wu for both raised mourning only three days.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan himself had stopped music after three days for two royal deaths in one year.

sentences.zh: 中興已後，更參論不改此制。

translations.literal: Since the Eastern Restoration courts have debated again and never altered that system.
translations.idiomatic: Jin restored that rule after the flight south and never changed it.

sentences.zh: 今小會宜作樂。

translations.literal: Therefore the small assembly ought use music."
translations.idiomatic: Wang concluded the solstice banquet could have music.'"

sentences.zh: 」二議竟不知所取。

translations.literal: Between the two opinions the court never settled which to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries left the contradiction unresolved.

sentences.zh: 《喪服記》，公為所寓，齊衰三月。

translations.literal: The Mourning Garments Record states that a lord for a host to whom he lodges wears qi-cui three months.
translations.idiomatic: Classical text still gives three months of qi-cui for a refugee lord and his patron.

sentences.zh: 新禮以今無此事，除此一章。

translations.literal: The New Rites deleted this chapter because the circumstance no longer occurs today.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's New Rites dropped the chapter as obsolete.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「《周禮》作于刑厝之時，而著荒政十二。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu argued: "The Zhou Rites were compiled when punishments were laid aside, yet they still list twelve famine policies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu said the Zhou compilers kept famine law even in peaceful times.'"

sentences.zh: 禮備制待物，不以時衰而除盛典，世隆而闕衰教也。

translations.literal: Rites complete their regulations to meet every contingency—they do not discard great ceremonies because the age declines, nor omit teachings on decline because the world prospers."
translations.idiomatic: Canon is written for hard cases, not shelved when peace returns.'"

sentences.zh: 曩者王司徒失守播越，自稱寄公。

translations.literal: When former Director Wang lost his command and wandered, calling himself a guest lord.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dao fled south and styled himself a dependent lord.'"

sentences.zh: 是時天下又多此比，皆禮之所及。

translations.literal: At that time many under Heaven were in the same case—all fell within ritual's reach.
translations.idiomatic: Half the court lived as exiled clients, exactly the case the classic addressed.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮自如舊經。

translations.literal: The New Rites should restore this chapter as in the old classic."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu asked to reinstate the old lodging-mourning article.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his view."
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.'"

sentences.zh: 漢魏故事無五等諸侯之制，公卿朝士服喪，親疏各如其親。

translations.literal: Han and Wei precedent had no five-rank feudal system; dukes, ministers, and court gentlemen wore mourning close or distant according to true kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei let mourning follow blood, not rank.

sentences.zh: 新禮王公五等諸侯成國置卿者，及朝廷公孤之爵，皆傍親絕期，而旁親為之服斬衰，卿校位從大夫者皆絕緦。

translations.literal: The New Rites hold that princes and dukes of the five ranks who have completed a state and installed ministers, together with court duke-and-guardian titles, all cut collateral mourning at qi, yet require collateral kin to wear zhan-cui for them, while ministers ranked with great officers cut si entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's code tried to sever collateral ties for great nobles while still demanding zhan-cui from cousins—a tangle Han never used.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「古者諸侯君臨其國，臣諸父兄，今之諸侯未同于古。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "Ancient feudal lords ruled their states and treated paternal uncles as subjects; today's nobles are not the same as antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu said Eastern Jin princes were not classical feudatories.'"

sentences.zh: 未同于古，則其尊未全，不宜便從絕期之制，而令傍親服斬衰之重也。

translations.literal: Because they are not the same as antiquity, their ritual supremacy is incomplete—it is not fitting to follow outright the rule that cuts qi while forcing collateral kin into zhan-cui."
translations.idiomatic: Weaker fiefs should not trigger the heaviest collateral weeds.'"

sentences.zh: 諸侯既然，則公孤之爵亦宜如舊。

translations.literal: Feudal lords being so, duke-and-guardian titles should likewise follow the old pattern."
translations.idiomatic: The same logic applied to titular dukes and tutors.'"

sentences.zh: 昔魏武帝建安中已曾表上，漢朝依古為制，事與古異，皆不施行，施行者著在魏科。

translations.literal: Wei Emperor Wu in the Jian'an era already memorialized for Han to legislate by antiquity; because affairs differed from antiquity, nothing was enacted, while what was enacted appears in Wei code.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's memorials show even Wei could not force archaic mourning on current facts.'"

sentences.zh: 大晉采以著令，宜定新禮皆如舊。

translations.literal: Great Jin adopted those entries into promulgated law—the New Rites ought everywhere to match the old statute."
translations.idiomatic: Jin had codified Wei's workable clauses and should keep them.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript accepted Zhi Yu.'"

sentences.zh: 《喪服》無弟子為師服之制，新禮弟子為師齊衰三月。

translations.literal: Mourning Garments contains no rule for disciples mourning teachers; the New Rites prescribe qi-cui three months for a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The revision added three months of qi-cui for masters.

sentences.zh: 摯虞以為：「自古無師服之制，故仲尼之喪，門人疑于所服。

translations.literal: Zhi Yu held: "From antiquity there was no teacher-mourning code—therefore at Confucius's death disciples were unsure what to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu noted Confucius's own funeral left disciples guessing.'"

sentences.zh: 子貢曰：『昔夫子之喪顏回，若喪子而無服，請喪夫子若喪父而無服。

translations.literal: Zigong said: 'When the Master mourned Yan Hui, it was like mourning a son but without mourning garments; I ask to mourn the Master like mourning a father but without mourning garments.'"
translations.idiomatic: Zigong recalled Confucius mourning Yan Hui like a son yet without hemp.'"

sentences.zh: 』遂心喪三年。

translations.literal: Thereupon they observed heart mourning three years.
translations.idiomatic: They settled on three years of inner grief without graded dress.

sentences.zh: 此則懷三年之哀，而無齊衰之制也。

translations.literal: That harbors three years of grief yet lacks a qi-cui regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Deep sorrow without a hemp schedule.

sentences.zh: 群居，入則絰，出則否，所謂弔服加麻也。

translations.literal: When assembled they wore zhui ties indoors but not outdoors—what is called adding hemp to condolence dress.
translations.idiomatic: In company they added hemp bands only inside the gate.

sentences.zh: 先聖為禮，必易從而可傳。

translations.literal: Former sages made ritual easy to follow and possible to transmit.
translations.idiomatic: The sages built rites people could actually keep.

sentences.zh: 師徒義誠重，而服制不著，歷代相襲，不以為缺。

translations.literal: Teacher-disciple duty is weighty, yet garment rules were never written down—later ages followed one another and did not treat that as a defect.
translations.idiomatic: No dynasty had spelled out teacher weeds, yet nobody called the silence a gap.

sentences.zh: 且尋師者以彌高為得，故屢遷而不嫌；

translations.literal: Moreover those who seek teachers take 'ever higher' as their gain—therefore they change masters repeatedly without scruple;
translations.idiomatic: Students chase better teachers and swap mentors freely.'"

sentences.zh: 修業者以日新為益，故舍舊而不疑。

translations.literal: those who pursue learning take 'daily renewal' as profit—therefore they cast aside the old without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship thrives by moving on, not by lifelong mourning for every tutor.'"

sentences.zh: 仲尼稱『三人行，必有我師焉』。

translations.literal: Zhongni said, 'In a party of three walking, there must be my teacher among them.'"
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said any trio could include a teacher.'"

sentences.zh: 子貢云，『夫何常師之有』。

translations.literal: Zigong said, 'What constant teacher is there?'"
translations.idiomatic: Zigong denied a single fixed master.'"

sentences.zh: 淺學之師，暫學之師，不可皆為之服。

translations.literal: Shallow teachers and brief teachers cannot all receive mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Not every instructor deserves a funeral grade.

sentences.zh: 義有輕重，服有廢興，則臧否由之而起，是非因之而爭，愛惡相攻，悔吝生焉。

translations.literal: When rightness has light and heavy and garments wax and wane, praise and blame arise, yes and no contend, love and hate clash, and regret is born.
translations.idiomatic: Codifying teacher mourning would only spark quarrels over rank and favor.

sentences.zh: 宜定新禮無服如舊。

translations.literal: The New Rites should leave teacher mourning absent, as in antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu asked to strike the new article and follow the silent precedent.'"

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this."
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.'"

sentences.zh: 古者天子諸侯葬禮粗備，漢世又多變革，魏晉以下世有改變，大體同漢之制。

translations.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven and feudal lords had roughly complete burial rites; Han introduced many changes; Wei and Jin later generations altered them again—the broad pattern still matched Han.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tombs grew more elaborate through Han and Jin.

sentences.zh: 而魏武以禮送終之制，襲稱之數，繁而無益，俗又過之，豫自制送終衣服四篋，題識其上，春秋冬夏，日有不諱，隨時以斂。

translations.literal: Yet Wei Wu held that the rites of sending off the dead and tallies of condolence gifts were excessive without benefit; vulgar practice exceeded them still—so he prepared in advance four chests of burial clothes, labeled for spring, summer, autumn, and winter, to be donned according to whichever season death came.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao loathed wasteful obsequies and packed four seasonal shrouds against an unlucky day.'"

sentences.zh: 金珥珠玉銅鐵之物，一不得送。

translations.literal: Gold, pearls, jade, copper, and iron were forbidden grave goods altogether.
translations.idiomatic: He banned metal and gems from the pit.'"

sentences.zh: 文帝遵奉，無所增加。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen followed this and added nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi kept his father's frugal will.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，刻金璽，追加尊號，不敢開埏，乃為石室，藏璽埏首，以示陵中無金銀諸物也。

translations.literal: When accepting abdication he carved a gold seal and added honor titles yet dared not open the tunnel—so he built a stone chamber at the passage mouth to store the seal, showing the tomb held no gold or silver.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi sealed a gold seal in a stone niche to prove the mound stayed bare of treasure.'"

sentences.zh: 漢禮明器甚多，自是皆省之矣。

translations.literal: Han burials had been rich in mingqi grave goods—from this point onward all were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Opulent Han figurines gave way to leaner Wei practice.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝，又自作終制曰：「禮，國君即位為椑，存不忘亡也。

translations.literal: Wei Wendi also personally composed an end testament saying: "By ritual a state lord on accession prepares an outer coffin—alive, he does not forget death."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi wrote his own will about prefabricated coffins and remembering mortality.'"

sentences.zh: 壽陵因山為體，無封樹，無立寢殿，造園邑，通神道。

translations.literal: His Shou mausoleum follows the mountain's contour—no mound, no trees, no resting hall, no park district, no spirit road opened.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted a lean tumulus cut into Shou hill without surface works.'"

sentences.zh: 夫葬者藏也，欲人之不得見也。

translations.literal: Burial means hiding—wishing men not to see.
translations.idiomatic: A tomb should hide the dead from view.

sentences.zh: 禮不墓祭，欲存亡不黷也。

translations.literal: Ritual forbids sacrifice at the grave—wishing the living and dead not to profane one another.
translations.idiomatic: Classical law barred tomb-side offerings to keep worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 皇后及貴人以下不隨王之國者，有終沒，皆葬澗西，前又已表其處矣。

translations.literal: Empresses and honored ladies who do not follow the prince to his fief and who die in the end are all buried west of the Jian River; I have already marked the ground."
translations.idiomatic: Secondary consorts who stayed in the capital were to share a simple plot west of the stream.'"

sentences.zh: 」此詔藏之宗廟，副在尚書、秘書、三府。

translations.literal: This edict was deposited in the ancestral temple; copies went to the Masters of Writing, Palace Library, and the Three Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Copies of the will rested in the temple and chief ministries.'"

sentences.zh: 明帝亦遵奉之。

translations.literal: Ming-di likewise followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rui obeyed the same will.

sentences.zh: 明帝性雖崇奢，然未遽營陵墓之制也。

translations.literal: Though Ming-di's nature inclined to luxury, he still did not rush to build an extravagant mausoleum system.
translations.idiomatic: Even the lavish Cao Rui held back on tomb scale.

sentences.zh: 宣帝豫自于首陽山為土藏，不填不樹，作《顧命終制》，斂以時服，不設明器。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan in advance prepared an earthen burial chamber on Mount Shouyang—no mound, no trees—and composed the 'Charge at Gu' end testament: shroud in seasonal clothes only, with no ming vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi dug a plain shaft on Shouyang, left the hill unmarked, and left written orders for everyday clothes and no grave goods.

sentences.zh: 景、文皆謹奉成命，無所加焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing and Emperor Wen both scrupulously obeyed the completed testament and added nothing to it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao kept Cao Pi's austere burial instructions to the letter.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，喪事制度又依宣帝故事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, the funeral regulations again followed Emperor Xuan's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi's obsequies copied Sima Yi's lean model.

sentences.zh: 武帝，文明王皇后崩，將合葬，開崇陽陵，使太尉司馬望奉祭，進皇帝密璽綬于便房神坐。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenming Wang of Emperor Wu was to be buried with him, they opened the Chongyang mausoleum, sent Grand Commandant Sima Wang to offer sacrifice, and carried the emperor's sealed jade seal and cords into the side chamber before the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: For Wang Yuanji's co-burial with Sima Yan the court reopened Chongyang and placed the imperial seal in the niche facing her tablet.

sentences.zh: 魏氏金璽，此又儉矣。

translations.literal: Wei's gold seal—another mark of frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Even the golden seal bespoke restraint.

sentences.zh: 江左初，元、明崇儉，且百度草創，山陵奉終，省約備矣。

translations.literal: Early in the southward court, Emperors Yuan and Ming prized simplicity; the hundred offices were still being founded, so imperial tombs stayed spare yet adequate.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled across the Yangzi, Sima Rui and Sima Shao kept burials modest while institutions were new.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸康七年，皇后杜氏崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh Xiankang year of Emperor Cheng, Empress Du died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Du of Cheng passed in 341.

sentences.zh: 詔外官五日一入臨，內官旦一入而已，過葬虞祭禮畢止。

translations.literal: An edict ordered outer officials to enter condolence only once every five days and inner staff once at dawn, ending once burial and the Yu rite were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers could wail only on that thin schedule until the post-burial service closed mourning.

sentences.zh: 有司奏，大行皇后陵所作凶門柏歷門，號顯陽端門。

translations.literal: The offices proposed building a funeral gate and cypress "calendar" portal for the late empress's mound, to be named the Xianyang gate.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry wanted a formal death-gate and cypress lintel named like a palace portal.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「門如所處。

translations.literal: The edict read: "Let the gate stand where proposed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the gate's placement.

sentences.zh: 凶門柏歷，大為煩費，停之。

translations.literal: Funeral gates and cypress calendars are extravagantly costly—suspend them."
translations.idiomatic: He vetoed the costly timber gateway.'"

sentences.zh: 」案蔡謨說，以二瓦器盛始死之祭，繫於木，裹以葦席，置庭中，近南，名為重，今之凶門是其象也。

translations.literal: Cai Mo explains that two earthen jars holding the first-death offerings were lashed to a frame, wrapped in reed matting, and set in the courtyard toward the south as a chong; today's funeral gate imitates that form.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Mo traced the "death gate" to the temporary chong bundle hung south of the yard.

sentences.zh: 禮，既虞而作主，今未葬，未有主，故以重當之。

translations.literal: By ritual one fashions the spirit tablet after the Yu rite; before burial there is no tablet, so the chong stands in for it.
translations.idiomatic: Until the tablet existed, the chong served as the spirit's lodging.

sentences.zh: 禮稱為主道，此其義也。

translations.literal: The canon calls this the "lord-of-the-spirit path"—that is the idea.
translations.idiomatic: Classical glosses treat the chong as the spirit's interim path.

sentences.zh: 范堅又曰：「凶門非禮，禮有懸重，形似凶門。

translations.literal: Fan Jian adds: "The funeral gate is not canonical; ritual only suspends a chong that merely resembles a gate."
translations.idiomatic: Fan Jian insisted the gate was folk imitation, not classical mourning gear.'"

sentences.zh: 後人出之門外以表喪，俗遂行之。

translations.literal: Later generations moved it outside the gate to advertise mourning, and vulgar custom adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: Vulgar practice dragged the chong out to the street as a billboard of grief.

sentences.zh: 薄帳，即古弔幕之類也。

translations.literal: Thin curtains belong to the ancient class of mourning screens.
translations.idiomatic: The plain hangings echoed old "condolence screens."

sentences.zh: 」是時，又詔曰：「重壤之下，豈宜崇飾無用，陵中唯潔掃而已。

translations.literal: Another edict then declared: "Beneath double layers of earth one should not lavish useless ornament; only sweep the vault clean."
translations.idiomatic: A follow-up rescript barred finery inside the shaft—clean earth only.'"

sentences.zh: 」有司又奏，依舊選公卿以下六品子弟六十人為挽郎，詔又停之。

translations.literal: The offices again asked to conscript sixty youths of sixth rank and below as catafalque pullers, as of old; the edict again refused.
translations.idiomatic: Officials wanted sixty noble sons as rope-pullers; the throne again said no.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝九月，皇后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of Emperor Xiaowu's reign Empress Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang died under Xiaowu,

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「終事唯從儉速。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Finish everything frugally and quickly."
translations.idiomatic: he ordered the funeral kept fast and plain.'"

sentences.zh: 」又詔：「遠近不得遣山陵使。

translations.literal: A further edict forbade dispatching tomb envoys from near or far.
translations.idiomatic: No courier was to be sent to the mausoleum on pretense of state business.'"

sentences.zh: 」有司奏選挽郎二十四人，詔停之。

translations.literal: When the ministry asked for twenty-four pullers, the edict stopped that as well.
translations.idiomatic: Even twenty-four rope-boys were denied.

sentences.zh: 古無墓祭之禮。

translations.literal: Antiquity knew no sacrifices at the tomb itself.
translations.idiomatic: The classics never sanctioned grave-side worship.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦，皆有園寢。

translations.literal: Han continued Qin and maintained park-like resting shrines at every imperial mound.
translations.idiomatic: Han kept Qin's tomb parks and resting halls.

sentences.zh: 正月上丁，祠南郊禮畢，次北郊、明堂、高廟、世祖廟，謂之五供。

translations.literal: On the upper ding day of the first month, after the southern suburban sacrifice, the court in sequence offered at the northern suburb, the Bright Hall, the High Temple, and Emperor Shizu's shrine—the so-called five offerings.
translations.idiomatic: The capital's spring round moved from the southern altar through the northern rites in fixed order.

sentences.zh: 魏武葬高陵，有司依漢立陵上祭殿。

translations.literal: Cao Cao was buried at Gaoling; the ministry, following Han, built a sacrificial hall atop the tumulus.
translations.idiomatic: Wei still raised a tomb-shrine over Gaoling, aping Han.

sentences.zh: 至文帝，乃詔曰：「先帝躬履節儉，遺詔省約。

translations.literal: When Wendi came to the throne, he issued an edict: "The late emperor lived frugally and his testament demanded austerity.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi cited Cao Cao's will to tear down the mound-top hall.'"

sentences.zh: 子以述父為孝，臣以繫事為忠。

translations.literal: The son expresses filial piety by carrying out the father's words; the minister shows loyalty by continuing his tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He framed obedience as filial duty and bureaucratic fealty.'"

sentences.zh: 古不墓祭，皆設於廟。

translations.literal: The ancients never sacrificed at graves—everything was set in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Canon placed all cult at the temple, not the pit.'"

sentences.zh: 高陵上殿皆毀壞，車馬還廄，衣服藏府，以從先帝儉德之志。

translations.literal: Destroy the upper halls at Gaoling; return carriages and horses to the stables and store garments in the treasury, to match the late emperor's wish for thrift."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi ordered Gaoling's shrine dismantled and the regalia locked away.'"

sentences.zh: 」文帝自作終制，又曰「壽陵無立寢殿，造園邑」，自後園邑寢殿遂絕。

translations.literal: Wendi's own testament added that his Shou mausoleum should have no resting hall and no tomb park—after that, tomb parks and mound halls ceased.
translations.idiomatic: His Shou-ling instructions ended Wei tomb parks for good.'"

sentences.zh: 齊王在位九年，始一謁高平陵而曹爽誅，其後遂廢，終於魏世。

translations.literal: The prince of Qi reigned nine years before he once visited Gaoling; after Cao Shuang's execution the practice was abandoned for the rest of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Fang's single visit to Gaoling ended with Cao Shuang's purge, and Wei rulers stopped touring tombs.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝，遺詔「子弟群官皆不得謁陵」。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan's testament commanded that "sons, younger kin, and all officials must not visit the imperial tombs."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi forbade kinsmen and ministers from grave pilgrimage.'"

sentences.zh: 於是景、文遵旨。

translations.literal: Jing and Wen obeyed that order.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shi and Sima Zhao complied.

sentences.zh: 至武帝，猶再謁崇陽陵，一謁峻平陵，然遂不敢謁高原陵，至惠帝復止也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu still visited Chongyang twice and Junping once, yet never dared approach Gaoling; under Emperor Hui the custom lapsed again.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan alone made limited visits, never to Cao Cao's mound, and Hui abandoned the habit entirely.

sentences.zh: 逮于江左，元帝崩後，諸公始有謁陵辭告之事。

translations.literal: After the move south of the Yangzi, not until Emperor Yuan died did high nobles begin visiting mausoleums to announce their leave-takings.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin nobles only began tomb pilgrimages after Sima Rui's death.

sentences.zh: 蓋由眷同友執，率情而舉，非洛京之舊也。

translations.literal: They acted from private friendship among peers, not from Luoyang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The practice sprang from camaraderie's impulse, not old capital law.

sentences.zh: 成帝時，中宮亦年年拜陵，議者以為非禮，於是遂止，以為永制。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Cheng the inner palace yearly visited tombs until critics called it uncanonical; the court then banned it permanently.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's harem stopped annual tomb trips once ritualists objected.

sentences.zh: 至穆帝時，褚太后臨朝，又拜陵，帝幼故也。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Mu, Empress Dowager Chu regent, tombs were visited again because the boy emperor was young.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's regent mother revived the visits while the sovereign was a child.

sentences.zh: 至孝武崩，驃騎將軍司馬道子曰：「今雖權制釋服，至於朔望諸節，自應展情陵所，以一周為斷。

translations.literal: After Xiaowu died, Sima Daozi said: "Though we have shortened mourning by expedient rule, on new and full moons and festivals we should still show feeling at the tomb—take one round as the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Daozi wanted monthly pilgrimages during shortened mourning.'"

sentences.zh: 」於是至陵，變服單衣，煩黷無準，非禮意也。

translations.literal: Thereupon courtiers went to the tombs in thin single garments—endless fuss with no standard, contrary to ritual intent.
translations.idiomatic: The result was slovenly dress and chaotic etiquette at every visit.'"

sentences.zh: 及安帝，尚書左僕射桓謙奏：「百僚拜陵，起于中興，非晉舊典，積習生常，遂為近法。

translations.literal: Under Emperor An, Huan Qian memorialized that mass tomb visits began at the Restoration, not from Jin's old code, and hardened into custom.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian traced the fad to the refugee court, not Western Jin statute.'"

sentences.zh: 尋武皇帝詔，乃不使人主諸王拜陵，豈唯百僚！

translations.literal: Review Emperor Wu's edict: he forbade even the sovereign and princes from tomb visits—let alone mere officials!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yan had barred the throne itself from the mounds.'"

sentences.zh: 謂宜遵奉。

translations.literal: We ought to obey that precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Huan asked the court to revert to Sima Yan's ban.'"

sentences.zh: 」於是施行。

translations.literal: The measure was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The ban took effect.

sentences.zh: 及義熙初，又復江左之舊。

translations.literal: Early in the Yixi era the southern custom briefly returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yixi reopened tomb pilgrimages for a time.

sentences.zh: ，大鴻臚鄭默母喪，既葬，當依舊攝職，固陳不起，於是始制大臣得終喪三年。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] When Chief Herald Zheng Mo's mother died, he should by precedent have returned to duty after burial, but he refused to rise; then the court first allowed great ministers to complete three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Mo's refusal to leave mourning forced Jin to grant grandees full three-year leave.'"

sentences.zh: 然元康中，陳準、傅咸之徒，猶以權奪，不得終禮，自茲已往，以為成比也。

translations.literal: Yet during Yuankang, Chen Zhun, Fu Xian, and others were still pressed by state business and could not finish ritual; thereafter that became the precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Even after the rule, Yuankang ministers were "urged" back early, and the exception became norm.'"

sentences.zh: ，東平王楙上言，相王昌父毖，本居長沙，有妻息，漢末使入中國，值吳叛，仕魏為黃門郎，與前妻息死生隔絕，更娶昌母。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] Prince Mao of Dongping reported: Chancellor Wang Chang's father Wang Bi had lived in Changsha with wife and children; late Han sent him inland, he met Wu's rebellion, served Wei as a Yellow Gate gentleman, and lost contact with his first family, then married Chang's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mao introduced Wang Bi: a Changsha household cut off by war who remarried in Wei and fathered Wang Chang.'"

sentences.zh: 今江表一統，昌聞前母久喪，言疾求平議。

translations.literal: Now that the lands south of the Yangzi are reunited, Wang Chang, learning that his first wife died long ago, pleads illness and seeks a neutral court ruling.
translations.idiomatic: With the south pacified, Wang Chang asked how to mourn a first wife presumed dead for decades.'"

sentences.zh: 守博士謝衡議曰：「雖有二妻，蓋有故而然，不為害於道，議宜更相為服。

translations.literal: Acting erudite Xie Heng argued: "Though there were two wives, there was good cause; it does not harm the Way—they should wear mutual mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Heng said both marriages were honest and each side deserved weeds.'"

sentences.zh: 」守博士許猛以為「地絕，又無前母之制，正以在前非沒則絕故也。

translations.literal: Acting erudite Xu Meng held: "Land cut-off means there is no rite for a former wife—the prior bond ends because she was not dead yet was severed."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Meng denied any mourning for the abandoned first wife.'"

sentences.zh: 前母雖在，猶不應服。

translations.literal: Even if the first wife still lived, Chang should not wear mourning for her."
translations.idiomatic: He barred mourning even were she alive.'"

sentences.zh: 」段暢、秦秀、騶沖從猛。

translations.literal: Duan Chang, Qin Xiu, and Zou Chong sided with Xu Meng.
translations.idiomatic: A bloc followed Xu Meng.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍劉智安議：「禮為常事制，不為非常設也。

translations.literal: Cavalier attendant Liu Zhi'an said: "Ritual governs the normal, not the extreme; the canon does not list parents whose fate is unknown."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi'an said classical mourning never covered unknown survival.'"

sentences.zh: 亡父母不知其死生者，不著於禮。

translations.literal: For parents whose death is unknown, the classics set down no mourning rule.
translations.idiomatic: He noted the canon never prescribes garments when one cannot know whether parents live or die.'"

sentences.zh: 平生不相見，去其加隆，以期為斷。

translations.literal: If they never met in life, drop the heaviest grades and stop at the one-year term."
translations.idiomatic: He capped grief at qi when kin never shared a roof.'"

sentences.zh: 」都令史虞溥議曰：「臣以為禮不二嫡，所以重正，非徒如前議者防妒忌而已。

translations.literal: Capital clerk Yu Pu said: "Ritual forbids two principal wives to secure orthodoxy—not merely to prevent jealousy.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu framed the issue as bigamy, not jealousy.'"

sentences.zh: 故曰『一與之齊，終身不改』，未有遭變而二嫡。

translations.literal: Hence the line 'once pledged together for life, never to change'—there is no provision for two lawful consorts after upheaval."
translations.idiomatic: The wedding vow assumes one legal spouse.'"

sentences.zh: 苟不二，則昌父更娶之辰，是前妻義絕之日也。

translations.literal: If bigamy is forbidden, the day Bi remarried was the day his first wife's tie ended in law."
translations.idiomatic: Remarriage itself dissolved the first match.'"

sentences.zh: 使昌父尚存，二妻俱在，必不使二嫡專堂，兩婦執祭，同為之齊也。

translations.literal: Had Bi lived with both wives present, the law would never let two matrons share the hall or both lead sacrifice as equals."
translations.idiomatic: Classical law could not seat two duchesses as co-equals.'"

sentences.zh: 」秦秀議：「二妾之子，父命令相慈養，而便有三年之恩，便同所生。

translations.literal: Qin Xiu argued: "When a father orders concubines' sons to foster one another, three years of grace appear—yet that equals birth only by decree.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xiu mocked extending concubine foster rules to rival principal wives.'"

sentences.zh: 昌父何義不命二嫡依此禮乎！

translations.literal: Why should Bi not order two principals to follow the same rule if that is so righteous!"
translations.idiomatic: He asked why Wang Bi could not decree dual duchesses if foster logic applied.'"

sentences.zh: 父之執友有如子之禮，況事兄之母乎！

translations.literal: A father's sworn friend receives almost filial rites—how much more a brother's mother!"
translations.idiomatic: He invoked the courtesy owed a father's bosom friend.'"

sentences.zh: 」許猛又議：「夫少婦稚，則不可許以改娶更適矣。

translations.literal: Xu Meng rejoined: "You cannot let a young wife and infant be cast off for remarriage elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Meng warned against abandoning toddlers to remarry.'"

sentences.zh: 今妻在許以更聘，夫存而妻得改醮者，非絕而何。

translations.literal: If a living husband may take another match while the wife remains, that is nothing but severance."
translations.idiomatic: A new betrothal with the first wife alive is divorce in fact.'"

sentences.zh: 」侍中領博士張惲議：「昔舜不告而娶，婚禮蓋闕，故《堯典》以釐降二女為文，不殊嫡媵。

translations.literal: Palace attendant and erudite Zhang Yun cited Shun's unannounced marriages: the Canon of Yao only records the two daughters sent down without distinguishing principal from secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun likened the case to Shun's dual match without naming an empress.'"

sentences.zh: 傳記以妃夫人稱之，明不立正后也。

translations.literal: Later texts call them consorts and ladies, showing no principal empress was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary styles them consorts, not a single queen.'"

sentences.zh: 夫以聖人之弘，帝者嫡子，猶權事而變，以定典禮。

translations.literal: Even sages and imperial heirs adjusted ritual to circumstance to fix the code.
translations.idiomatic: Sages bent the letter when human facts demanded it.'"

sentences.zh: 黃昌之告新妻使避正室，時論許之。

translations.literal: Huang Chang ordering his new wife to vacate the main chamber was praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: Han clerk Huang Chang's solution drew contemporary approval.'"

sentences.zh: 推姬氏之讓，執黃卿之決，宜使各自服其母。

translations.literal: Extrapolating from the Ji clan's deference and Huang's verdict, each son should mourn only the mother who raised him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun concluded each brother owed weeds only to his own mother.'"

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎崔諒、荀悝、中書監荀勖、領中書令和嶠、侍郎夏侯湛皆如溥議。

translations.literal: Cui Liang, Xun Kui, Xun Xu, He Qiao, and Xia Hou Zhan concurred with Yu Pu.
translations.idiomatic: A majority backed Yu Pu's bigamy reading.'"

sentences.zh: 侍郎山雄、兼侍郎著作陳壽以為：「溥駁一與之齊，非大夫也，禮無二嫡，不可以並耳。

translations.literal: Shan Xiong and Chen Shou replied that Yu Pu misread "once pledged"—the rule forbids two principals at once, not sequential marriages.
translations.idiomatic: They distinguished simultaneous wives from remarriage after loss.'"

sentences.zh: 若昌父及二母於今各存者，則前母不廢，已有明徵也。

translations.literal: If Bi and both mothers were alive today, the first wife would not be dismissed—that is already clear proof.
translations.idiomatic: They argued alive co-wives would change the calculus.'"

sentences.zh: 設令昌父將前母之子來入中國尚在者，當從出母之服。

translations.literal: Were Bi to bring the first wife's son inland while she lived, the son would follow "divorced mother" mourning.
translations.idiomatic: A living first mother would trigger the divorced-mother grade.'"

sentences.zh: 苟昌父無棄前妻之命，昌兄有服母之理，則昌無疑於不服。

translations.literal: If Bi never repudiated the first wife and the elder brother owes a mother's mourning, Wang Chang need not doubt that he wears none."
translations.idiomatic: They separated the elder brother's duty from Chang's.'"

sentences.zh: 」賊曹屬卞粹議：「昌父當莫審之時而娶後妻，則前妻同之于死而義不絕。

translations.literal: Bian Cui of the thieves section argued: "Bi wed his second wife in ignorance of the first's fate, so the first wife is as if dead yet the bond is not morally cut."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Cui said wartime ignorance kept the first marriage alive in principle.'"

sentences.zh: 若生相及而後妻不去，則妾列於前志矣。

translations.literal: If both lived and the second did not leave, she ranked as concubine in earlier law.
translations.idiomatic: Survival would demote the newcomer to concubine.'"

sentences.zh: 死而會乎，則同祔於葬，無並嫡之實。

translations.literal: If they died and were buried together, joint burial annexes her without making two principals.
translations.idiomatic: Co-burial annexes a concubine, not elevates her.'"

sentences.zh: 必欲使子孫於沒世之後，追計二母隔絕之時，以為並嫡，則背違死父，追出亡母。

translations.literal: Forcing later generations to call both principals after decades apart would betray the dead father and expel the vanished mother."
translations.idiomatic: Retroactive bigamy slandered both parents.'"

sentences.zh: 議者以為禮無前母之服者，可謂以文害意。

translations.literal: Critics who say ritual lacks a former-wife garment harm the meaning with dry text."
translations.idiomatic: Bian rejected literalism that erased real kinship.'"

sentences.zh: 愚以為母之不親而服三年，非一無異於前母也。

translations.literal: In my humble view, wearing three years for a distant mother is not the same as none for a prior wife."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng entered the fray on gradations of grief.'"

sentences.zh: 倉曹屬衛恆議：「或云，嫡不可二，前妻宜絕。

translations.literal: Wei Heng of the granary section said: "Some say two principals cannot stand—the first must be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng summarized rival extremes.'"

sentences.zh: 此為奪舊與新，違母從子，禮律所不許，人情所未安也。

translations.literal: That seizes the old for the new and makes the son annul his mother—ritual law and human feeling both forbid it."
translations.idiomatic: He called that reading cruel and illegal.'"

sentences.zh: 或云，絕與死同，無嫌二嫡，據其相及，欲令有服。

translations.literal: Others equate severance with death and allow two principals, then argue both alive to impose mourning—principal logic dies while garment logic lives, contradicting itself."
translations.idiomatic: He exposed self-contradiction in another school.'"

sentences.zh: 此為論嫡則死，議服則生，還自相伐，理又不通。

translations.literal: Some argue that when debating principal rank she counts as dead, yet when discussing garments they treat her as alive—those positions undercut each other and cannot both stand."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng highlighted the internal contradiction in that line of argument.'"

sentences.zh: 愚以為地絕死絕，誠無異也，宜一如前母，不復追服。

translations.literal: I hold land-severance and death-severance are the same: treat her like a former wife and do not impose retroactive mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Heng would grant no retroactive weeds after decades apart.'"

sentences.zh: 」主簿劉卞議：「毖在南為邦族，於北為羈旅，以此名分言之，前妻為元妃，後婦為繼室。

translations.literal: Chief clerk Liu Bian said: "In the south Bi was a clansman, in the north a traveler—by that status the first wife was primary consort, the later a successor chamber."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bian ranked the Changsha wife as primary by migration law.'"

sentences.zh: 何至王路既通，更當逐其今妻，廢其嫡子！

translations.literal: How, once imperial roads reopened, could we expel the present wife and disinherit her son!"
translations.idiomatic: He asked why reunification should annul the Wei marriage.'"

sentences.zh: 不書姜氏，絕不為親，以其犯至惡也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn omits Jiang because severance means no kin—she committed supreme evil.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the disowned Jiang clan as analogy.'"

sentences.zh: 趙姬雖貴，必推叔隗；

translations.literal: Though Lady Zhao was honored, she yielded to Shu Ji; though Yuan Tong was favored, Xuan Meng stayed principal.
translations.idiomatic: He invoked Zhao Dun's mother yielding to Shu Sui's precedent.'"

sentences.zh: 原同雖寵，必嫡宣孟。

translations.literal: If we violate ritual for a specious compromise, how does that match what the Spring and Autumn praises!"
translations.idiomatic: He appealed to the Annals' moral judgments.'"

sentences.zh: 若違禮苟讓，何則《春秋》所當善也！

translations.literal: Debaters cite land cut-off to say feeling could never cross.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the geography argument.'"

sentences.zh: 論者謂地絕，其情終已不得往來。

translations.literal: Now the land is linked—why insist on severance!"
translations.idiomatic: Reunion removed the excuse for bigamy.'"

sentences.zh: 今地既通，何為故當追而絕之邪！

translations.literal: Huang Chang is praised as a recent parallel worth imitating.'"
translations.idiomatic: He ended with the Eastern Han exemplar Huang Chang.'"

sentences.zh: 黃昌見美，斯又近世之明比。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Prince of Qi Sima You cited the Record of Rites: "Those born too late to reach grandparents, paternal uncles, or elder brothers—when the father eases mourning, they do not"—the ru all explain that the father, for some other reason, bore the son in a distant land and did not return in time to see these kin alive; though the father may don eased mourning, the son does not follow the easing—not demanding favor out of season."
translations.idiomatic: Sima You opened with the "late-born child" passage: a son born abroad need not match a father's retroactive mourning.'"

sentences.zh: 司空齊王攸議：「《禮記》『生不及祖父母、諸父昆弟，而父稅喪，己則否』，諸儒皆以為父以他故子生異域，不及此親存時歸見之，父雖追服，子不從稅，不責非時之恩也。

translations.literal: Yet if they never even met, one still does not ease mourning for those who died earlier—how much more a former mother not of the same womb: righteousness does not climb past ancestors, neither coming nor going, grace uniquely severed—yet ordering retroactive mourning hardly fits what we call weighing feeling to set the text.
translations.idiomatic: Never having shared a roof weighs more heavily than a distant cousin; a stepmother-by-war cannot demand the same thread as a birth mother.

sentences.zh: 但不相見，尚不服其先終，而況前母非親所生，義不逾祖，莫往莫來，恩絕殊隔，而令追服，殆非稱情立文之謂也。

translations.literal: He concluded that Wang Chang ought not pursue retroactive mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Sima You ruled Chang should wear no added mourning for the first wife.

sentences.zh: 以為昌不宜追服。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Li Yin argued: "When Bi served as Yellow Gate Gentleman, south of the Yangzi had already rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin's memorial began: Wang Bi held a Wei post while Wu still held the south.'"

sentences.zh: 」司徒李胤議：「毖為黃門侍郎，江南已叛。

translations.literal: "Shi Hou joined the plot—great righteousness may destroy kin—how much more under Bi's circumstances can she be treated as a lawful wife!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin cited the Spring and Autumn principle that kin who abet rebellion are struck down, asking how Wang Bi's first marriage could survive that standard.'"

sentences.zh: 石厚與焉，大義滅親，況於毖之義，可得以為妻乎！

translations.literal: Shi Hou joined the plot—great righteousness may destroy kin—how much more under Wang Bi's moral position can she be treated as a lawful wife!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yin finished: Shi Hou aided treason, and the canon approves destroying kin for righteousness—Wang Bi's first match cannot still count as wife.

sentences.zh: 」大司馬騫不議，太尉充、撫軍大將軍汝南王亮皆從主者。

translations.literal: ' Grand Marshal Sima Qian offered no opinion; Grand Commandant Jia Chong, Commander-in-chief General of the Guard the Prince of Runan, Liang, and others all followed the supervisor's recommendation.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Sima Qian stayed silent while Jia Chong and Sima Liang backed the drafters.'"

sentences.zh: 溥又駁粹曰：「喪從甯戚，謂喪事尚哀耳，不使服非其親也。

translations.literal: Yu Pu again refuted Bian Cui: "Mourning follows easing grief—it means funerals esteem sorrow, not that one wears mourning for someone who is not kin.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pu said 'mourning follows grief' bars garments for people who are no longer kin.'"

sentences.zh: 夫死者終也，終事已故無絕道。

translations.literal: Death is the end; once the affair is finished there is no principle of endless tie.'
translations.idiomatic: Death closes the ritual account; nothing mandates an endless bond.'"

sentences.zh: 分居兩存，則離否由人。

translations.literal: If the two households live apart and both survive, then separation or union lies in human choice.'
translations.idiomatic: While both sides live, staying together or parting is a human decision.'"

sentences.zh: 夫婦以判合為義，今土隔人殊，則配合理絕。

translations.literal: Husband and wife join by ritual union; now earth divides them and persons differ—then the match is logically severed.'
translations.idiomatic: Physical separation severs the ritual marriage.'"

sentences.zh: 彼已更娶代己，安得自同於死婦哉！

translations.literal: The other party has remarried in her place—how can she equate herself with a dead wife!
translations.idiomatic: A new wife has replaced her; she cannot act the buried corpse.'"

sentences.zh: 伯夷讓孤竹，不可以為後王法也。

translations.literal: Boyi yielding Guzhu cannot be taken as precedent for later kings.'
translations.idiomatic: Boyi's abdication is no model for modern marriage law.'"

sentences.zh: 且既已為嫡後服，復云為妾，生則或貶或離，死則同祔于葬，妻專一以事夫，夫懷貳以接己，開偽薄之風，傷貞信之教，於以純化篤俗，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, having already worn mourning as principal heir, to say one is still a concubine—alive she may be demoted or divorced, dead buried together—while the wife serves one husband faithfully and the husband keeps two hearts toward her—this opens hypocrisy, wounds faithful teaching, and makes pure custom hard indeed!
translations.idiomatic: He warned that demoting a living principal to concubine while the husband keeps two hearts corrupts chastity teaching.'"

sentences.zh: 今昌二母雖土地殊隔，據同時並存，何得為前母后母乎！

translations.literal: Now Wang Chang's two mothers, though lands divide them, existed at the same time—how can you call one former and one later!
translations.idiomatic: Both women were alive together, so 'first' and 'second' mislabels them.'"

sentences.zh: 設使昌母先亡，以嫡合葬，而前母不絕，遠聞喪問，當復相為制何服邪！

translations.literal: Suppose Chang's mother died first and was buried as principal while the first wife's line never ended—news of mourning arrives from afar—what garment rule would then apply between them!
translations.idiomatic: He posed the impossible case of two tombs and conflicting mourning signals.'"

sentences.zh: 夫制不應禮，動而愈失。

translations.literal: Regulations that violate ritual move further from right the more they are used.'
translations.idiomatic: Rules that fight the canon only deepen error.'"

sentences.zh: 夫孝子不納親於不義，貞婦不昧進而苟容。

translations.literal: A filial son does not admit kin into unrighteousness; a chaste wife does not advance by conniving tolerance.'
translations.idiomatic: Sons and wives cannot be enlisted in unjust schemes.'"

sentences.zh: 今同前嫡於死婦，使後妻居正而或廢，於二子之心，曾無恧乎！

translations.literal: Now you equate the former principal with a dead woman while letting the later wife hold orthodox rank or be cast aside—could the two sons feel no shame!
translations.idiomatic: He asked whether sons could stomach demoting a living mother.'"

sentences.zh: 而云誣父棄母，恐此文致之言，難以定臧否也。

translations.literal: To speak of slandering father and abandoning mother is probably prosecutorial language—hard to use it to judge guilt.'
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed inflammatory charges of disowning parents.'"

sentences.zh: 禮，違諸侯適天子，不服舊君，然則昌父絕前君矣，更納後室，廢舊妻矣，又何取於宜誅宜撫乎！

translations.literal: By ritual, when a feudal lord goes to the Son of Heaven he does not wear mourning for his old lord—then Wang Bi's father had already cut ties with his former prince, taken a new chamber, and dismissed the first wife—why cite cases fit for execution or clemency!
translations.idiomatic: He compared Bi's remarriage to the rule that lords cease mourning for old rulers when serving the Zhou king.'"

sentences.zh: 且婦人之有惡疾，乃慈夫之所愍也，而在七出，誠以在人理應絕故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when a wife has vile disease it is what a kind husband pities—yet it is listed among the seven expulsions because human principle demands severance.'
translations.idiomatic: Even pitiable illness can justify divorce under the seven grounds.'"

sentences.zh: 今夫婦殊域，與無妻同，方之惡疾，理無以異。

translations.literal: Now husband and wife live in different realms—no different from having no wife—compared with vile disease there is no distinction in principle.'
translations.idiomatic: Permanent separation matches the seven-expulsion logic.'"

sentences.zh: 據己更娶，有絕前之證。

translations.literal: According to his own remarriage there is proof the first tie was cut.'
translations.idiomatic: Bi's new marriage itself proves the first bond ended.'"

sentences.zh: 而云應服，于義何居！

translations.literal: Yet you say he should wear mourning—where is the rightness in that!"
translations.idiomatic: He asked how mourning could still be owed.'"

sentences.zh: 」尚書八座以為「設令有人于此，父為敦煌太守，而子後任于洛，若父娶妻，非徒不見，乃可不知，及其死亡，不得不服。

translations.literal: ' The Eight Seats of the Masters of Writing held: "Suppose someone here whose father was governor of Dunhuang while the son later serves in Luoyang: if the father remarries, not only might the son never see her—he might not even know; when she dies he must still wear mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Eight Seats imagined a son ignorant of a father's new wife yet still owing her weeds.'"

sentences.zh: 但鞠養已者情哀，而不相見名制，雖戚念之心殊，而為之服一也。

translations.literal: Yet toward the one who nursed him he feels grief, while toward the unseen stranger only name and ritual apply—though the stir of feeling differs, the garment grade is one.'
