translations.idiomatic: They argued grief differs but the mourning grade stays unified.'"

sentences.zh: 又，兩后匹嫡，自謂違禮，不謂非常之事而以常禮處之也。

translations.literal: Moreover, two empresses ranking as principals was itself deemed contrary to ritual—not an extraordinary case to handle with everyday rubrics.'
translations.idiomatic: They rejected applying ordinary two-wife logic to the two-empress anomaly.'"

sentences.zh: 昔子思哭出母於廟，其門人曰：『庶氏之女死，何為哭于孔氏之廟！

translations.literal: Formerly Zisi wailed for his divorced mother inside the temple; his disciples said, 'When a daughter of the Shu line died, why wail in Kong's temple!'
translations.idiomatic: They cited Zisi moving his mother's lament out of the Confucian shrine.'"

sentences.zh: 』子思懼，改哭於他室。

translations.literal: ' Zisi feared and shifted his wailing to another chamber.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zisi moved the rite to a side room.'"

sentences.zh: 若昌不制服，不得不告其父祖，掘其前母之尸，徙之他地。

translations.literal: If Chang wears no mourning, he would have to tell his father and grandfather, exhume the first mother's corpse, and move it elsewhere.'
translations.idiomatic: They threatened that refusing mourning forces removal of the first burial.'"

sentences.zh: 若其不徙，昌為罪人。

translations.literal: If they do not move her, Chang becomes a criminal.'
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the body in place would make Chang lawbreaker.'"

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?'
translations.idiomatic: They asked the rhetorical why.'"

sentences.zh: 異族之女不得祔于先姑，藏其墓次故也。

translations.literal: Because a woman of another clan may not be buried with a mother-in-law—that is why she cannot share the tomb row.'
translations.idiomatic: Alien kin cannot share a mother-in-law's niche in the lineage grave.'"

sentences.zh: 且夫婦人牽夫，猶有所尊，趙姬之舉，禮得權通，故先史詳之，不譏其事耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, a wife follows her husband yet still has superiors to honor—Lady Zhao's promotion was a sanctioned expedient, which is why earlier historians recorded it without blame.'
translations.idiomatic: They cited Lady Zhao's precedence as a controlled exception.'"

sentences.zh: 今昌之二母，各已終亡，尚無並主輕重之事也。

translations.literal: Now Chang's two mothers are both dead—there is no longer a question of two living principals.'
translations.idiomatic: Death removed the dual-spouse problem.'"

sentences.zh: 昌之前母，宜依叔隗為比。

translations.literal: Chang's first mother should be compared to Shu Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: They analogized her to Shu Ji.'"

sentences.zh: 若亡在昌未生之前者，則昌不應復服。

translations.literal: If she died before Chang was born, Chang need not wear mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: No mourning if she predeceased the son.'"

sentences.zh: 生及母存，自應如禮以名服三年。

translations.literal: If she was alive when he was born, he follows the canonical three-year term by name.'
translations.idiomatic: Living overlap triggers full three-year weeds.'"

sentences.zh: 輒正定為文，章下太常報楙奉行。」

translations.literal: They therefore fixed the text in writing and sent it down to the Chamberlain for Ceremonials for Mao to execute.'
translations.idiomatic: They finalized wording for the ritual office.'"

sentences.zh: 制曰：「凡事有非常，當依準舊典，為之立斷。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Whenever an affair is extraordinary, one must rely on old canons and render a decision.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne demanded precedent for irregular cases.'"

sentences.zh: 今議此事，稱引趙姬、叔隗者粗是也。

translations.literal: Now in debating this matter, citing Lady Zhao and Shu Ji is roughly right.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict conceded the Zhao–Shu parallel was apt in outline.'"

sentences.zh: 然後狄與晉和，故姬氏得迎叔隗而下之。

translations.literal: But then the Di made peace with Jin, so the Ji lady could welcome Shu Ji and rank her below herself.'
translations.idiomatic: Peace allowed the two Di wives to order themselves ritually.'"

sentences.zh: 吳寇隔塞，毖與前妻，終始永絕。

translations.literal: Wu rebels blocked the roads—Wang Bi and his first wife were forever severed.'
translations.idiomatic: Warfare unlike the Di case made the first marriage a dead letter.'"

sentences.zh: 必義無兩嫡，則趙衰可以專制隗氏。

translations.literal: If righteousness forbids two principals, then Zhao Dun could have monopolized the Lady of the Di line.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict noted Zhao Dun could not have kept two principals under law.'"

sentences.zh: 昌為人子，豈得擅替其母。

translations.literal: As a son, how could Chang on his own replace his mother!"
translations.idiomatic: A son cannot unilaterally demote a parent.'"

sentences.zh: 且毖二妻並以絕亡，其子猶後母之子耳，昌故不應制服也。」

translations.literal: Moreover, both of Bi's wives are dead; the sons are children of the later mother only—Chang therefore should not wear mourning for the first.'
translations.idiomatic: The rescript denied Chang any mourning for the first wife.'"

sentences.zh: 太興初，著作郎干寶論之曰：「禮有經有變有權，王毖之事，有為為之也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taixing, Editorial Director Gan Bao reflected: "Ritual has constant, adaptive, and expedient levels—Wang Bi's affair was handled with motive.'
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao called the case a deliberate expedient, not a textbook precedent.'"

sentences.zh: 有不可責以始終之義，不可求以循常之文，何群議之紛錯！

translations.literal: Some cases cannot be judged by rules from cradle to grave, nor squeezed into ordinary text—why so many tangled opinions!"
translations.idiomatic: He marveled at the swarm of contrary memorials.'"

sentences.zh: 同產者無嫡側之別，而先生為兄；

translations.literal: Those born of the same mother have no distinction of principal versus secondary—yet the elder is called brother;
translations.idiomatic: He began with siblings of one womb: the elder is simply 'brother.'"

sentences.zh: 諸侯同爵無等級之差，而先封為長。

translations.literal: Among feudal lords of equal rank there is no gradation—yet the first enfeoffed is treated as senior.'
translations.idiomatic: He added the parallel of coequal lords: first enfeoffment marks seniority.'"

sentences.zh: 今二妻之入，無貴賤之禮，則宜以先後為秩，順序義也。

translations.literal: Now when two wives enter a house without ritual ranking of noble versus base, precedence should follow order of entry—this matches orderly rightness.'
translations.idiomatic: He proposed resolving co-wives by order of arrival.'"

sentences.zh: 今生而同室者寡，死而同廟者眾，及其神位，固有上下也。

translations.literal: In life few today share one roof; in death many share one temple—so for spirit tablets there is naturally an upper and lower.'
translations.idiomatic: Shrines already rank tablets high and low.'"

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》賢趙姬遭禮之變而得禮情也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn praises Lady Zhao for meeting a ritual anomaly with humane feeling.'
translations.idiomatic: He praised Zhao Ji for navigating ritual change humanely.'"

sentences.zh: 且夫吉凶哀樂，動乎情者也，五禮之制，所以敘情而即事也。

translations.literal: Moreover, auspicious and inauspicious, grief and joy, are stirred by feeling; the five rites exist to order feeling and fit the affair.'
translations.idiomatic: He tied the five rites to emotional ordering.'"

sentences.zh: 今二母者，本他人也，以名來親，而恩否于時，敬不及生，愛不及喪，夫何追服之道哉！

translations.literal: Now the two mothers were originally strangers; they became 'kin' only by name, while affection waxed or waned with the hour—reverence never reached them in life, love never reached them in death—what principle demands retroactive mourning!"
translations.idiomatic: He denied retroactive weeds for women who never formed a true bond.'"

sentences.zh: 張惲、劉卞，得其先後之節，齊王、衛恆，通於服絕之制，可以斷矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Yun and Liu Bian grasped the precedence of first and last; the Prince of Qi and Wei Heng understood when mourning rightly ends—on that the case may be decided.'
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao endorsed Zhang, Liu, Sima You, and Wei Heng.'"

sentences.zh: 朝廷於此，宜導之以趙姬，齊之以詔命，使先妻恢含容之德，後妻崇卑讓之道，室人達長少之序，百姓見變禮之中。

translations.literal: The court here should guide them with Lady Zhao's example, align them with edicts, let the first wife practice tolerant virtue, the later wife practice yielding humility, household members grasp senior and junior order, and the people see adaptation within change.'
translations.idiomatic: He urged the state to model tolerance and yielding.'"

sentences.zh: 若此，可以居生，又況於死乎！

translations.literal: If that can govern the living, how much more the dead!"
translations.idiomatic: What works for the living surely governs the dead.'"

sentences.zh: 古之王者，有以師友之禮待其臣，而臣不敢自尊。

translations.literal: Ancient kings treated ministers with teacher-and-friend courtesy, yet ministers dared not presume on it.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited kings' modesty toward ministers.'"

sentences.zh: 今令先妻以一體接後，而後妻不敢抗，及其子孫交相為服，禮之善物也。

translations.literal: Now let the first wife receive the later wife as one body, while the later wife dares not resist; let their grandsons exchange mourning garments—this is ritual's finest fruit.'
translations.idiomatic: He imagined mutual recognition between lines.'"

sentences.zh: 然則王昌兄弟相得之日，蓋宜祫祭二母，等其禮饋，序其先後，配以左右，兄弟肅雍，交酬奏獻，上以恕先父之志，中以高二母之德，下以齊兄弟之好，使義風弘于王教，慈讓洽乎急難，不亦得禮之本乎！」

translations.literal: Then on days when Wang Chang's brothers gather, they should jointly sacrifice to both mothers, equalize offerings, order precedence, seat tablets left and right; brothers in harmony would alternate toasts, satisfying the late father's intent, honoring both mothers' virtue, and knitting brotherly affection—spreading dutiful custom through royal instruction and kindly yielding through crisis—is that not ritual's root!"
translations.idiomatic: Gan Bao's peroration envisioned joint sacrifice and brotherly harmony.'"

sentences.zh: 是時，沛國劉仲武先娶毌丘氏，生子正舒、正則二人。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Zhongwu of Pei first married a daughter of the Guqiu clan and bore sons Zhengshu and Zhengzhe.'
translations.idiomatic: He introduced Liu Zhongwu's first marriage to Guqiu.'"

sentences.zh: 毌丘儉反敗，仲武出其妻，娶王氏，生陶，仲武為毌丘氏別舍而不告絕。

translations.literal: When Guqiu Jian rebelled and fell, Zhongwu cast out his wife and married Lady Wang, bearing Tao; he housed the Guqiu separately but never formally severed ties.'
translations.idiomatic: He told how Zhongwu hid a continuing tie to the first wife.'"

sentences.zh: 及毌丘氏卒，正舒求祔葬焉，而陶不許。

translations.literal: When Guqiu died, Zhengshu asked to bury her by attachment, but Tao refused.'
translations.idiomatic: The half-brothers quarreled over co-burial.'"

sentences.zh: 舒不釋服，訟於上下，泣血露骨，縗裳綴絡，數十年弗得從，以至死亡。

translations.literal: Shu refused to shed mourning, sued up and down, wept blood and exposed bone, patching hemp for decades until death without winning his suit.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhengshu's lifelong lawsuit failed.'"

sentences.zh: 時吳國朱某娶妻陳氏，生子東伯。

translations.literal: In Wu, a man Zhu took wife Chen and bore Dongbo.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited Wu precedents.'"

sentences.zh: 入晉，晉賜妻某氏，生子綏伯。

translations.literal: Entering Jin, Jin granted him another wife and bore Suibo.'
translations.idiomatic: A Jin-bestowed second wife followed.'"

sentences.zh: 太康之中，某已亡，綏伯將母以歸邦族，兄弟交愛敬之道，二母篤先後之序，雍雍人無間焉。

translations.literal: In Taikang, when the first had died, Suibo brought his mother home to the lineage; brothers practiced mutual love and respect, the two mothers honored order of seniority, and the household was harmonious without rancor.'
translations.idiomatic: He praised a harmonious two-mother household.'"

sentences.zh: 及其終也，二子交相為服，君子以為賢。

translations.literal: When they died, the two sons wore mourning for each other's mothers—gentleman deemed them worthy.'
translations.idiomatic: Cross-mourning earned praise.'"

sentences.zh: 安豐太守程諒先已有妻，後又娶，遂立二嫡。

translations.literal: Cheng Liang, prefect of Anfeng, already had a wife, then married again, thus setting up two principals.'
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Liang's double-primary case opened a new query.'"

sentences.zh: 前妻亡，後妻子勳疑所服。

translations.literal: When the first wife died, the later wife's son Xun doubted what to wear.'
translations.idiomatic: Xun asked about mourning grades.'"

sentences.zh: 中書令張華造甲乙之問曰：「甲娶乙為妻，後又娶丙，匿不說有乙，居家如二嫡，無有貴賤之差。

translations.literal: Prefect of the Masters of Writing Zhang Hua posed a paired question: "A took B as wife, later took C, hiding that B existed—he lived as if with two principals of equal rank.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua's hypothetical posed hidden bigamy.'"

sentences.zh: 乙亡，丙之子當何服？

translations.literal: When B died, what should C's son wear?
translations.idiomatic: The question targeted the hidden first wife's death.'"

sentences.zh: 本實並列，嫡庶不殊，雖二嫡非正，此失在先人，人子何得專制析其親也。

translations.literal: In truth both stood coequal; principal and secondary were not distinguished—though two principals are irregular, the fault lies with the elders; how may a child on his own sever kin!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua blamed fathers, not sons.'"

sentences.zh: 若為庶母服，又不成為庶。

translations.literal: If he wears mourning for a concubine-mother, he cannot really be a concubine son.'
translations.idiomatic: The grades contradict if he takes concubine mourning.'"

sentences.zh: 進退不知所從。

translations.literal: He cannot decide whether to advance or retreat.'
translations.idiomatic: The heir is caught between grades.'"

sentences.zh: 」太傅鄭沖議曰：「甲失禮於家，二嫡並在，誠非人子所得正。

translations.literal: ' Grand Tutor Zheng Chong answered: "A failed ritual at home—two principals present—is not something a child may correct.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Chong said sons cannot fix parental bigamy.'"

sentences.zh: 則乙丙之子並當三年，禮疑從重。

translations.literal: Then sons of both B and C should wear three years; when ritual doubts, follow the heavier.'
translations.idiomatic: He chose three years for both lines.'"

sentences.zh: 」車騎賈充、侍中少傅任愷議略與鄭同。

translations.literal: General of Chariots and Cavalry Jia Chong and Palace Attendant Junior Tutor Ren Kai largely agreed with Zheng.'
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong and Ren Kai concurred.'"

sentences.zh: 太尉荀顗議曰：「《春秋》並后匹嫡，古之明典也。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Xun Yi answered: "The Spring and Autumn treats two coequal empresses as a clear mirror of error.'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Yi cited the two-empress precedent as warning.'"

sentences.zh: 今不可以犯禮並立二妻，不別尊卑而遂其失也。

translations.literal: Today one cannot break ritual to keep two wives; one must not blur noble and base and perpetuate the fault.'
translations.idiomatic: He forbade prolonging the error.'"

sentences.zh: 故當斷之以禮，先至為嫡，後至為庶。

translations.literal: Therefore ritual must decide: first arrival is principal, later is secondary.'
translations.idiomatic: He ordered first wife principal, second secondary.'"

sentences.zh: 丙子宜以嫡母服乙，乙子宜以庶母事丙。

translations.literal: C's son should mourn B as principal mother; B's son should serve C as secondary mother.'
translations.idiomatic: He split mourning directions by generation.'"

sentences.zh: 昔屈建去芰，古人以為違禮而得禮。

translations.literal: Formerly Qu Jian cast aside water caltrop—ancients thought him wrong on the letter yet right on ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: He cited Qu Jian's symbolic act.'"

sentences.zh: 丙子非為抑其親，斯自奉禮先後貴賤順敘之義也。

translations.literal: C's son is not belittling kin—he follows the sequence of ritual precedence.'
translations.idiomatic: He defended the secondary line.'"

sentences.zh: 」中書監荀勖議曰：「昔鄉里鄭子群娶陳司空從妹，後隔呂布之亂，不復相知存亡，更娶鄉里蔡氏女。

translations.literal: ' Director of the Palace Secretariat Xun Xu answered: "Formerly Zheng Ziqun of the village married a cousin of Director Chen; later, separated by Lu Bu's chaos, he could not learn whether she lived, and remarried a Cai woman in the village.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Xun Xu cited Zheng Ziqun's two-wife survival case.'"

sentences.zh: 徐州平定，陳氏得還，遂二妃並存。

translations.literal: When Xuzhou was pacified, the Chen lady returned—then both consorts coexisted.'
translations.idiomatic: Peace reunited both wives.'"

sentences.zh: 蔡氏之子字元釁，為陳氏服嫡母之服，事陳公以從舅之禮。

translations.literal: The Cai son, styled Yuanxin, wore principal mourning for the Chen lady and served Director Chen by the courtesy due a maternal uncle.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxin honored the returned first wife.'"

sentences.zh: 族兄宗伯曾責元釁，謂抑其親，鄉里先達以元釁為合宜。

translations.literal: A senior kinsman once reproached Yuanxin for belittling kin, yet village worthies approved him.'
translations.idiomatic: Village elders backed Yuanxin's choice.'"

sentences.zh: 不審此事粗相似否。」

translations.literal: He asked whether the present case is broadly similar.'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu invited comparison to Wang Chang.'"

sentences.zh: ，以溫嶠為散騎侍郎，嶠以母亡值寇，不臨殯葬，欲營改葬，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: [The narrative continues:] Wen Jiao was appointed cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.'
translations.idiomatic: The court named Wen Jiao cavalier attendant-in-ordinary.'"

sentences.zh: 元帝詔曰：「溫嶠不拜，以未得改卜葬送，朝議又頗有異同。

translations.literal: Because his mother had died amid bandits he could not attend encoffining, he wished to relocate burial and firmly declined the commission.'
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded to move her grave and refused the post until burial was settled.'"

sentences.zh: 為審由此邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's edict said: "Wen Jiao does not accept commission because he has not been able to relocate and bury his mother; court debate still differs.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted divided opinion on Wen Jiao.'"

sentences.zh: 天下有闕塞，行禮制物者當使理可經通。

translations.literal: Is it truly for that reason?'
translations.idiomatic: He asked the motive behind the refusal.'"

sentences.zh: 古人之制三年，非情之所盡，蓋存亡有斷，不以死傷生耳。

translations.literal: When the realm is blocked, those who set ritual must keep principle navigable.'
translations.idiomatic: He demanded flexible ritual in wartime.'"

sentences.zh: 要絰而服金革之役者，豈營官邪？

translations.literal: The ancients' three years is not the limit of feeling—it marks where life and death divide so the living are not destroyed by the dead.'
translations.idiomatic: He explained the three-year limit.'"

sentences.zh: 隨王事之緩急也。

translations.literal: Those who gird hemp yet take up arms are not scheming office—they follow the urgency of royal business.'
translations.idiomatic: He compared wartime service to hemp-clad soldiers.'"

sentences.zh: 今桀逆未梟，平陽道斷，奉迎諸軍猶未得徑進，嶠特一身，于何濟其私艱，而以理閡自疑，不服王命邪！

translations.literal: Now the rebel has not been beheaded, the road to Pingyang is cut, the armies escorting the court still cannot advance straight in—Jiao is alone; how does tending private hardship block him from obeying the kingly command!"
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Wen Jiao to serve despite burial delay.'"

sentences.zh: 其令三司八座、門下三省、外內群臣，詳共通議如嶠比，吾將親裁其中。

translations.literal: Order the Three Departments, Eight Seats, Chancellery and three inner bureaus, and inner and outer ministers to deliberate jointly on cases like Jiao's—I will personally decide the mean.'
translations.idiomatic: He convened a plenary session on such cases.'"

sentences.zh: 」於是太宰、西陽王羕，司徒臨潁公組，驃騎將軍、即丘子導，侍中紀瞻，尚書周顗，散騎常侍荀邃等議，以「昔伍員挾弓去楚，為吳行人以謀楚，誠志在報仇，不苟滅身也。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the grand tutor, Prince Yang of Xiyang, the minister of education the duke of Linying, Zu, the general of agile cavalry, viscount of Qiqiu, Dao, the palace attendant Ji Zhan, minister Zhou Yi, and cavalier attendant Xun Sui jointly argued that "when Wu Yuan carried his bow and left Chu to serve Wu as envoy plotting against Chu, his intent was revenge, not self-destruction.'
translations.idiomatic: ' High ministers cited Wu Zixu's loyal vendetta.'"

sentences.zh: 溫嶠遭難，昔在河朔，日尋干戈，志刷讎惡，萬里投身，歸赴朝廷，將欲因時竭力，憑賴王威，以展其情，此乃嶠之志也。

translations.literal: When Wen Jiao suffered calamity, north of the Yellow River he daily took up arms, intent on wiping out his foe; he crossed ten thousand li to reach court, wishing to seize the moment and exhaust his strength, trusting royal majesty to vent his heart—that was Jiao's intent.'
translations.idiomatic: They likened Wen Jiao's flight to Wu Zixu's loyalty.'"

sentences.zh: 無緣道路未通，師旅未進，而更中辭王事，留志家巷也。

translations.literal: It is not that roads were still blocked and armies had not marched, yet he set aside royal business midcourse and fixed his mind on home lanes.'
translations.idiomatic: They denied he was merely dodging duty.'"

sentences.zh: 以為誠宜如明詔。

translations.literal: They held it truly fitting to follow the clear edict.'
translations.idiomatic: They urged accepting the imperial order.'"

sentences.zh: 」於是有司奏曰：「案如眾議，去九月下辛未令書，依禮文，父喪未葬，唯喪主不除。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon the offices memorialized: "Reviewing the consensus, remove the ninth-month xinwei edict; by ritual text, while a father's corpse is unburied only the chief mourner does not remove mourning.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The bureaucracy memorialized to rescind the earlier edict and keep the chief mourner in weeds until burial.'"

sentences.zh: 以他故未葬，人子之情，不可居殯而除，故期於畢葬，無遠近之斷也。

translations.literal: Because he has not been buried, the love for the Son of Man cannot be extinguished during the funeral. Therefore, there is no separation between the distance and the near after the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Because he has not been buried, the love for the mourning son cannot be extinguished during the funeral; Therefore, there is no separation between the distance and the near after the funeral;.

sentences.zh: 若亡遇賊難，喪靈無處，求索理絕，固應三年而除，不得故從未葬之例也。

translations.literal: If the deceased is in trouble due to thieves, and the deceased has nowhere to go, and seeks explanation, he should be exterminated within three years, and there is no reason why he should never be buried.
translations.idiomatic: If the dead is in trouble due to thieves, and the dead has nowhere to go, and seeks explanation, he should be exterminated within three years, and there is no reason why he should never be buried;.

sentences.zh: 若骨肉殲於寇害，死亡漫于中原，而繼以遺賊未滅，亡者無收殯之實，存者又闕於奔赴之禮，而人子之情，哀痛無斷，輒依未葬之義，久而不除，若遂其情，則人居無限之喪，非有禮無時不得之義也。

translations.literal: If the flesh and bones are annihilated by the bandits, death spreads over the Central Plains, and the remaining thieves are still alive, the deceased will not be able to be buried, and the survivors will not be able to rush to the ceremony. However, the love for the son of man will never be cut off, and the grief will not be cut off, and he will always rely on the meaning of not being buried for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: If the flesh and bones are annihilated by the bandits, death spreads over the Central Plains, and the remaining thieves are still alive, the dead will not be able to be buried, and the survivors will not be able to rush to the ceremony; However, the love for the son of man will never be cut off, and the grief will not be cut off, and he will always rely on the meaning of not being buried for a long time;.

sentences.zh: 諸如此，皆依東關故事，限行三年之禮畢而除也。

translations.literal: All these are based on the story of Dongguan, and the rituals are limited to three years before being eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: All these are based on the story of Dongguan, and the rituals are limited to three years before being eliminated;.

sentences.zh: 唯二親生離，吉凶未分，服喪則凶事未據，從吉則疑於不存，心憂居素，出自人情，有如此者，非官制之所裁。

translations.literal: Only when two relatives are separated, the good and bad are not divided. When mourning, the bad things are not confirmed. When the good is good, there is doubt about the absence. The heart is worried and it is out of human feelings. Such people are not ruled by the official system.
translations.idiomatic: Only when two relatives are separated, the good and bad are not divided; When mourning, the bad things are not confirmed; When the good is good, there is doubt about the absence; The heart is worried and it is out of human feelings; Such people are not ruled by the official system;.

sentences.zh: 今嶠以未得改卜奔赴，累設疾辭。

translations.literal: Today, Qiao has not been able to change the divination and rushed to it, leaving many excuses.
translations.idiomatic: Today, Qiao has not been able to change the divination and rushed to it, leaving many excuses;.

sentences.zh: 案辛未之制，已有成斷，皆不得復遂其私情，不服王命，以虧法憲。

translations.literal: The system of the case Xinwei has been concluded, and no one can resume his personal relationship, disobey the king's order, and violate the law and the constitution.
translations.idiomatic: The system of the case Xinwei has been concluded, and no one can resume his personal relationship, disobey the king's order, and violate the law and the constitution;.

sentences.zh: 參議可如前詔嶠受拜，重告以中丞司徒，諸如嶠比者，依東關故事辛未令書之制。

translations.literal: The counselor can be worshiped like the previous imperial edict to Qiao, and then report to the Zhongcheng Situ again, such as Qiao Bi, according to the Dongguan Story Xinwei Order.
translations.idiomatic: The counselor can be worshiped like the previous imperial edict to Qiao, and then report to the Zhongcheng Situ again, such as Qiao Bi, according to the Dongguan Story Xinwei Order;.

sentences.zh: 」嶠不得已，乃拜。

translations.literal: Qiao had no choice but to worship.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao had no choice but to worship;.

sentences.zh: 是時中原喪亂，室家離析，朝廷議二親陷沒寇難，應制服不。

translations.literal: At that time, the Central Plains was in chaos and the family was separated. The court discussed whether the two relatives should be subdued if they were trapped by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, the Central Plains was in chaos and the family was separated; The court discussed whether the two relatives should be subdued if they were trapped by the bandits;.

sentences.zh: 太常賀循曰：二親生離，吉凶未分，服喪則凶事未據，從吉則疑於不存，心憂居素，允當人情。
